topics.title: SWE-smith Harbor packages expose the fix through git history in the agent container
topics.body:
The SWE-smith Harbor task packages in `DCAgent/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s` (and the same layout in `mlfoundations-dev/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests`) leave the repository's full git history in the agent's container. The image built from `environment/Dockerfile` keeps a local `main` branch with the unbroken code and about 944 other branches, so the agent can print the fix with `git diff HEAD main -- <package>` or `git show main:<file>`. `/tests` and `/solution` are correctly absent from the image.

Reproduce: build `swesmith-00003`'s `environment/Dockerfile` from the package, run it with no network, then `git log --oneline` (three commits: Initial commit, Bug Patch, Remove F2P Tests), `git branch -a` (944 branches including `main`), `git diff HEAD main -- oauthlib` (the exact fix).

Impact on existing data: in `open-athena/Kimi-2.5-swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s-maxeps-32k`, 860 of 5,237 passing trials (16.4%) and 433 of 4,119 failing trials run history-reading commands (`git show main:<path>`, diffs against `main` or `HEAD~N`, checkout or restore from history, `git log -p`). Some are benign (a diff against `HEAD~1` shows only the removed tests); many copy the original file. So the reported pass rate on these packages is inflated, and trace sets built on them carry shortcut solutions: the Kimi set above, the `GLM-4.7` and AgentTrove swesmith streams, and the allkimi relay data (`laion/calibforge-relay-traces`, `kimi_swesmith` rows) that was DARE-grafted into Snowball v0 (`open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Merge-Campaign3-DARE-Linear-02-2026.10.12`). SWE-bench Verified is not affected: there the fix is not in the repository's past.

A plain squash is not enough, because `tests/test.sh` itself uses history (`git checkout <task branch>; git checkout HEAD~1`) to restore the removed fail-to-pass tests before running pytest.

Expected: during the agent phase the repository has one commit, no other branches, no remote and no reflog; the verifier restores the fail-to-pass tests from outside the agent's view (for example, ship the test files in `tests/` and copy them in, or keep a git bundle that only the verifier unpacks). For each task, the gold patch still passes, the unpatched repository still fails, and the history-reading commands above return nothing.

Done when: a fixed package build exists with that validation on a sample of tasks, existing SWE-smith pass rates and training sets built on the leaky packages are re-reported with history-reading trials removed or flagged, and the shootout pool in #10213 uses the fixed packages.

comments.body:
🤖

# Research

The reported `swesmith-00003` image retains the pre-bug `main` branch and earlier commits, so an agent can recover the fix from Git history. Removing old refs alone is insufficient if the object database still contains the clean tree; the current verifier also uses `HEAD~1` to recover fail-to-pass tests. The reported 860/5,237 passing and 433/4,119 failing history-reading trials are contamination candidates, not yet an audited count of trials that copied the fix. Marin consumes these external packages and traces, while the package builder is outside this checkout.

**Relevant code and artifacts**
- [DCAgent package release](https://huggingface.co/datasets/DCAgent/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s) — affected task source.
- [Shootout #10213](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10213) — waits for stripped packages.
- [AgentTrove ingestion](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/agenttrove.py#L17) — SWE-smith trace consumer.
- [Relay source PR #10027](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10027) — registers Kimi SWE-smith rows.

# Proposal

## Outcome

Publish an immutable, revision-pinned Harbor package release whose agent image contains the bugged working tree in one new Git repository with one commit, one task branch, no `main`/remote/tags/reflog, and no recoverable old objects. Keep the fail-to-pass test payload in Harbor's verifier-only `tests/` area and copy it into the repository when scoring. Record the old and new package revisions and per-task content digests; do not overwrite the release used by existing trials.

## Plan

1. Change the package producer to create a fresh `.git` after applying each bug patch, rather than squashing the existing repository in place. Export required test files from the source package into verifier-only storage before discarding history. Make `tests/test.sh` restore those files without `git checkout` or `HEAD~1`; keep `solution/` and `tests/` out of the agent container.
2. Validate a stratified sample across repositories and test layouts in offline Harbor runs. In each agent image, require one reachable commit and no old refs, remotes, reflogs, or dangling objects containing the clean fix. Exercise `git show main:<file>`, `git diff HEAD main -- <package>`, `git show HEAD~1`, `git log -p`, and `git fsck --unreachable`; none may reveal the clean file. For each sampled task, the untouched bugged tree must score 0 and the gold patch must score 1 under the revised verifier. Publish task IDs, package digests, commands, and results with the new release.
3. Audit the Kimi, GLM-4.7, AgentTrove, and allkimi relay/Snowball v0 provenance at trial or row level. Classify history commands as benign inspection, fix recovery, or unresolved; report raw and unflagged success rates with denominators, plus counts by outcome and category. Publish flagged row IDs or a reproducible manifest and clean-filtered trace revisions where the source can be republished. Annotate existing model and dataset results; filtering rows cannot undo training already performed on Snowball v0.
4. Pin the fixed package revision in the #10213 SWE-smith pool and block the eight-attempt generation until the package validation passes. Keep the already stated pilot-trace history filter separate from the new pool validation. Coordinate Harbor release acquisition with [#10198](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10198); its cache work does not repair the package contents.

## Risks and open questions

The package producer and release permissions are external to this repository, so the new dataset revision needs an owner with access to that build pipeline. The verifier payload must be checked against every sampled task's required test files; a one-commit image can still give false rewards if a file is omitted. Excluding all history-reading trials gives a conservative subset, not an unbiased replacement for a fresh evaluation on fixed packages.

🤖 A fresh GLM 5.3 trial on the raw package used the history to check its fix.

**Setup:** `swesmith-00003` from `DCAgent/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s` (revision 78b0d879), unchanged. Harbor at `marin-community/harbor@016dd78b`, mini-swe-agent 2.1.0 with a 32k context, Daytona sandbox, GLM 5.3 through the internal bulk service. The trial passed (reward 1, 16 model calls).

**History use in the trajectory:**
- Step 6: `git log --oneline -5 && git status` showed `Remove F2P Tests` / `Bug Patch` / `Initial commit`.
- Step 8: `git log --all --oneline -- oauthlib/oauth2/rfc8628/endpoints/device_authorization.py && git show 614b134:oauthlib/oauth2/rfc8628/endpoints/device_authorization.py`. The second command prints the pre-bug file (`614b134` is `Initial commit`).
- Step 17: `git diff 614b134 -- oauthlib/oauth2/rfc8628/endpoints/device_authorization.py && echo "IDENTICAL TO ORIGINAL"` printed `IDENTICAL TO ORIGINAL`. The agent confirmed that its edit matches the original file before submitting.

GLM made the edit itself at step 10, after reading the original file at step 8. So this pass is history-assisted, and a GLM pass rate on these packages would be inflated in the same way as the Kimi data.

**Visibility probe:** an oracle-agent probe printed the container state during the agent phase (no model calls).
- `/testbed`: 944 branches (`main`, the task branch, `remotes/origin/*` for every task), and `git log --all` lists every task's `Bug Patch` / `Remove F2P Tests` commits.
- `/tests`: absent.
- `/solution`: absent for model agents. Harbor uploads it only for the oracle agent.
- None of the other task files are present (`task.json`, `test_*_state.py`, `setup.sh`, `container.def`, `test_state.py`).

**Run folders:** `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/sft-shootout/generation/dryrun/swe-dry3` (trajectory: `swesmith-00003__LQ7xGdF/attempts/000/agent/trajectory.json`) and `.../dryrun/visibility1`.

**Consequence for the SFT-shootout teacher pilot (#10213):** the SWE-smith 200x2 pass-rate pilot will run only on the history-stripped packages.

🤖 Fixed SWE-smith packages for the #10213 pool, with validation on 20 tasks. The same class of leak is also present in TMax.

**Fixed packages.** `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/sft-shootout/pool/swesmith-packages.parquet` (sha256 `f004b109edf8aa9274693c07e01266d14469ec8c61fe695cc516aa1175117407`), 2,100 tasks. The schema is the same as the DCAgent parquet (`path`, `task_binary`), and the folder names are unchanged. The source is `DCAgent/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s@78b0d879`. The upstream dataset is not modified. Code: [`experiments/post_training/sft_shootout_pool/`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/3bc613878c/experiments/post_training/sft_shootout_pool) on branch `task/206`.

- `environment/Dockerfile`: after the upstream `git fetch && git checkout <instance>`, the same `RUN` replaces the repository: `rm -rf .git && git init && git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/main && git add -A && git commit -m "Initial commit" && git reflog expire --expire=now --all && git gc --prune=now`. This is a new `.git`, not a squash, so no old objects remain in the container's filesystem. The base image's lower layers still hold the old `.git`, but the container cannot read them.
- `tests/f2p_restore/`: the files that the upstream `git checkout HEAD~1` would change, at their parent contents, plus `deleted.txt`. They are computed from a bare clone of `github.com/swesmith/<repo>`. On `swesmith-00003` they match the image's own `git show HEAD~1:<path>` byte for byte.
- `tests/test.sh`: `git checkout <instance>; git checkout HEAD~1;` is replaced by `cp -a /tests/f2p_restore/files/. /testbed/` plus the deletions. The rest is unchanged. Harbor uploads `tests/` only to the verifier (checked in harbor 0.24.0 `verifier/verifier.py`; only `agents/oracle.py` uploads `solution/`).

**Validation** on 20 pool tasks, one from each of 20 repos, in local Docker following Harbor's phase order:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Agent-phase repository: 1 commit, 1 branch, 0 remotes, empty reflog, no `HEAD~1`/`main~1`/`origin/main`/`master` | 20/20 |
| Gold patch (`solution/solve.sh`) then `tests/test.sh`: reward 1 | 20/20 |
| Unpatched tree: reward 0 | 19/20 |
| Leak commands (`git log --all -p`, `git show HEAD~1`, `git diff HEAD main`, `git diff HEAD~1`, `git fsck --unreachable --lost-found`, `git stash list -p`, `git show main:<every file>`) print a clean-only line | 0/20 (upstream `swesmith-00003` control: 2/2) |

- `swesmith-01094` (`ariga/atlas`) also scores 1 unpatched with the unmodified upstream package, so its verifier does not detect the bug. This is an upstream defect, and it means DCAgent's "oracle verified" does not imply that an unpatched run fails.
- "Clean-only line": a source line the Bug Patch removed that occurs nowhere in the bugged tree. 7 of the 20 tasks have none, so only the ref checks apply to them.
- The filesystem search found no git leak. It did find copies of clean lines in installed packages: `setuptools/_vendor/typeguard` is an older vendored typeguard, which is relevant for `agronholm/typeguard` tasks (57 in the pool). The `_pytest` (iniconfig) and `rapidfuzz` (thefuzz) hits are probably coincidental.
- Residual: `github.com/swesmith/<repo>` is public and keeps every instance branch, so an agent with internet access can still fetch the fix. In the Kimi traces this happened once (`git fetch origin; git show origin/main:<file>`).

Per-task results: `pool/swesmith-validation-20.jsonl` and `pool/swesmith-leak-probe-20.jsonl`.

**TMax: same class of leak, different mechanism.** In `allenai/TMax-SFT-16.5K@848e2182` `tasks.zip`, 221 of 2,200 environments build verifier assets into the agent's image (for example `/opt/oracle/<reference program>`, `/app/verifier/ground_truth_valid_events.txt`, `/home/user/oracle.py`), and `test_final_state.py` reads them. In 181 of the 221, the instruction never names the path. In the #202 Qwen3.6-27B success traces (`allenai/tmax-sft`), 63 trajectories across 18 tasks name one of these hidden paths in a bash command. That is a heuristic: naming a path doesn't prove the answer was copied. The pool excludes the 181 (`excluded.jsonl`, `leak_risk=hidden_verifier_assets`) and keeps the 40 visible ones. TMax's Harbor converter (`hamishivi/tmax@6d3d606c`) does not copy `task.json` (including its `truth` field), `solutions/`, `setup.sh` or `test_initial_state.py`; `test_final_state.py` goes only to `tests/`.

**Effect on #202's pilot training set:** 860 Kimi history-reading passes and those 63 TMax trajectories were removed before training (manifest `selection.swesmith_git_history_rule` and `selection.tmax_hidden_asset_rule`).

🤖 The public `github.com/swesmith` mirrors are now unreachable while the agent runs, and a second leak was found in mini-swe-agent's own install.

**TL;DR**
- During the agent phase, the sandbox can reach only the model proxy. github.com, PyPI, apt and every other host fail DNS, and direct-IP HTTPS (GitHub 140.82.112.3, 140.82.114.4; 1.1.1.1) has its TLS handshake cut. Setup and the verifier keep full network.
- mini-swe-agent 2.1.0 installs a tool env that the agent can read. It holds clean copies of three pool repos: pygments, pandas, tenacity. GLM read `tenacity/retry.py` from it and called it "the reference". The conda base in the images also holds boltons 23.0.0. All four repos (469 tasks) are excluded from pool P.

**Why not a whole-trial block:** Harbor sets the Daytona network policy once per sandbox. Both the mini-swe-agent install and the SWE-smith verifier (`tests/test.sh`) download uv from github.com releases (`astral.sh/uv/0.7.13/install.sh`), so a whole-trial allow-list without github.com breaks them.

**Mechanism** ([`harbor_agents/trial_agents.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1555295d4d5a233e1bb854c814b927c21889574c/experiments/post_training/sft_shootout/harbor_agents/trial_agents.py), `AgentPhaseNetwork`, branch `task/207` @ `1555295d`): just before the agent's run, the live sandbox is switched to `domain_allow_list=iris.oa.dev` (the proxy host). The run starts once that host resolves, and the task's own policy is restored before the verifier. Each trial writes the applied policy to `agent/agent_network.json`, and the run's `driver_config.json` records it under `agent_network`.

**Measured** (null agent on swesmith-00008, -00698, -00763; HTTPS HEAD from inside the sandbox):

| Target | Before | Agent phase | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| `https://github.com/swesmith` | 200 | DNS failure | 200 |
| `api.github.com`, `raw.githubusercontent.com`, `codeload.github.com` | 200 | DNS failure | 200 |
| `https://140.82.112.3/`, `https://140.82.114.4/` (GitHub by IP) | 200 | TLS handshake cut | 200 |
| `https://1.1.1.1/` | 403 | TLS handshake cut | 403 |
| `pypi.org`, `deb.debian.org`, `archive.ubuntu.com`, `www.google.com` | 200 | DNS failure | 200 |

On these unchanged trees the verifier completed afterwards and scored 0, as expected. With GLM (`swe-net2`), 3/3 trials passed under the limit, and all 76 proxy calls returned 200. In one trial GLM ran `pip install pytest ...` and saw `No internet`.

**Tool-env leak:** in `swe-net2/swesmith-00763` (jd/tenacity), GLM ran `sed -n '136,175p' /root/.local/share/uv/tools/mini-swe-agent/lib/python3.12/site-packages/tenacity/retry.py`. A probe ran mini-swe-agent's real setup on one task from each of the 36 repos (`toolenv2`). It found the same 80 distributions on every image. Only three of them are pool repos: pygments (222 tasks), pandas (196) and tenacity (30). Every conda-based image also ships conda's own `boltons-23.0.0` under `/opt/miniconda3/pkgs`, including the mahmoud/boltons image (21 tasks). The install is now pinned (`mini-swe-agent-2.1.0-constraints.txt`, sha256 `c67d1ee2…`, Python 3.12), so this set cannot drift between the pilot and the full run. SWE-smith ingestion also drops any trace whose commands or outputs touch `/root/.local/share/uv/tools/`.

**Run folders** (`s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/sft-shootout/generation/dryrun/`):
- `netprobe2`, `netprobe3`, `netprobe4`: network probes; `agent/network_probe.json` per trial.
- `swe-net2`: GLM trials under the limit.
- `toolenv2`: tool-env listing; union in `tool_env.json`.

🤖 More of the #10212 leak class: clean copies of the code the agent must fix, readable in the sandbox without git. The SWE-smith shootout pool is now at v4.

| Where | Found by | Pool repos affected |
|---|---|---|
| mini-swe-agent's own tool env, installed in the sandbox at agent setup (`/root/.local/share/uv/tools/mini-swe-agent/lib/python3.12/site-packages/`) | #207 run swe-net2: GLM read `tenacity/retry.py` there and called it "the reference". Then #207's probe ran mini-swe-agent's real setup with the pinned dependency set on one task per repo. | pygments, pandas, tenacity |
| conda's package cache in every conda image (`/opt/miniconda3/pkgs/boltons-23.0.0-*`) | the same #207 probe | boltons |
| pip/setuptools vendored copies and an installed egg in the base images | the base-image check: a suffix pass plus a name pass over every file outside `/testbed` | chardet, tomli, inflect, dataset |

What was removed in each version:

| Version | Repo or task | Tasks removed | Reason (`leak_risk`) | Where the clean copy lives |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| v1 | 181 TMax environments | 181 | `hidden_verifier_assets` | verifier assets (oracle programs, ground-truth files) built into the image, not named in the instruction |
| v2 | `agronholm/typeguard` | 57 | `vendored_clean_copy` | `setuptools/_vendor/typeguard` |
| v2 | `swesmith-01094` (`ariga/atlas`) | 1 | `broken_verifier` | (no copy: the verifier scores the unpatched tree 1, upstream too) |
| v3 | `pygments/pygments` | 222 | `agent_tool_clean_copy` | mini-swe-agent's tool env, `/root/.local/share/uv/tools/mini-swe-agent/lib/python3.12/site-packages/` (installed at agent setup) |
| v3 | `pandas-dev/pandas` | 196 | `agent_tool_clean_copy` | same |
| v3 | `jd/tenacity` | 30 | `agent_tool_clean_copy` | same |
| v3 | `mahmoud/boltons` | 21 | `image_level_clean_copy` | `/opt/miniconda3/pkgs/boltons-23.0.0-*/` (conda depends on boltons) |
| v4 | `chardet/chardet` | 10 | `image_level_clean_copy` | `pip/_vendor/chardet` (base env, conda pkgs, `/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages`) |
| v4 | `hukkin/tomli` | 23 | `image_level_clean_copy` | `pip/_vendor/tomli`, `setuptools/_vendor/tomli` (testbed env, base env, conda pkgs) |
| v4 | `jaraco/inflect` | 27 | `image_level_clean_copy` | `setuptools/_vendor/inflect` (testbed env, conda pkgs) |
| v4 | `pudo/dataset` | 13 | `image_level_clean_copy` | `dataset-1.6.2-py3.10.egg` in the testbed env site-packages |

Defenses now in place:

- **Pool:** every repo above is removed from pool v4. The SWE-smith family is topped back up to 2,100 from the 28 remaining repos, which the base-image check found clean. The method and per-repo evidence are in `image-check-v4.jsonl` and `manifest.json` `clean_copy_probe` (`s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/sft-shootout/pool/`, mirrored at [open-athena/Snowball-SFT-Shootout-Pool-2026.10@ac4e9c3f](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-SFT-Shootout-Pool-2026.10/tree/ac4e9c3fee6612c1d8ceecb0aa22950c4bdd8a9a)).
- **Generation (#207):** mini-swe-agent installs with a pinned dependency set, so the tool env cannot drift. The agent phase runs without internet access (proxy host only), which also closes the public `github.com/swesmith` mirrors.
- **Training rows (#211):** the row builder drops any trace that touches mini-swe-agent's tool env, or that reads a library copy (site-packages, `_vendor`, conda pkgs, the Go module cache) of its task's own repo. Drops are counted per task.

Kimi and other existing SWE-smith trace sets were generated with other agent setups, so their tool environments may differ. A trace audit for these paths is still open.

🤖 Upstream task defect found while freezing the SWE-smith shootout pool (v5). These 7 packages in `DCAgent/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s@78b0d879` have verifiers that cannot fail. The tree with the bug still in it scores 1. All 7 are in `paramiko/paramiko`. This is the same class as `swesmith-01094` above.

| Task | Repo |
|---|---|
| swesmith-06993 | paramiko/paramiko |
| swesmith-07209 | paramiko/paramiko |
| swesmith-07315 | paramiko/paramiko |
| swesmith-07539 | paramiko/paramiko |
| swesmith-07171 | paramiko/paramiko |
| swesmith-07599 | paramiko/paramiko |
| swesmith-07659 | paramiko/paramiko |

- **How they were found:** #207 ran a pool-wide null agent (it changes nothing) on all 2,100 fixed SWE-smith packages. 2,093 scored 0 and these 7 scored 1. Records: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/sft-shootout/generation/integrity/swe-{null,added-null}/integrity.jsonl`.
- **Not caused by the history fix:** the unmodified upstream packages were then run in local Docker in Harbor's phase order (`validate_swesmith.py`). All 7 score 1 unpatched, and the gold patch also scores 1. So the defect is in the upstream verifiers, not in the `tests/f2p_restore` change.
- **Action:** all 7 are removed from pool v5 as `broken_verifier` and replaced outcome-blind (#10213). Anyone else using this DCAgent release should drop them too: a policy gets reward 1 on them for doing nothing.

🤖 **TL;DR:** existing SWE-smith trace sets use the git-history leak. 16–18% of passing Kimi-2.5 traces read git history, and in 94% of the testable cases the output showed a line of the fix. The same holds for the 2,665 passing `kimi_swesmith` trials in `laion/calibforge-relay-traces`, which went into the allkimi relay SFT grafted into Snowball v0: 491 of them read git history.

| Set (revision) | Traces | Passes | Passes reading git history | ...that saw a fix line (testable) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `open-athena/Kimi-2.5-swesmith-...-maxeps-32k` (`1b87a9cf78`) | 9,356 | 5,237 | 860 (16.4%) | 708 / 752 (94%) |
| `laion/calibforge-relay-traces` `kimi_swesmith` (`66feab4d24`) | 4,392 | 2,665 | 491 (18.4%) | 418 / 446 (94%) |
| `DCAgent2/GLM-4.7-swesmith-...-maxeps-131k` (`e209a88db1`) | 9,437 | no verdicts | 848 of 8,241 completed (10.3%) | 723 / 790 (92%) |
| `open-thoughts/AgentTrove` swesmith rows (`b395a4307a`) | 78,246 | Kimi-2.5 stream only (same 5,237) | 5,822 of all traces (7.4%) | not testable (task ids differ) |

- **Commands:** most hits are `git diff HEAD~1 -- <file>`, `git show <hash>`, `git show main:<file>`, `git diff main` and `git log -p`.
- **"Saw a fix line":** the terminal output after the history command contains a clean-code line from the task's bug patch (15+ characters, in a non-test file) that the agent had not typed earlier.
- **Relay set's own flags:** its `leak` and `hunt` flags are False on all 4,392 rows, including these 491.
- **AgentTrove clone tasks:** 40,590 of AgentTrove's swesmith rows (the GLM-4.6, GPT 5.1 Nano and Kimi K2.0 streams, and part of GLM-4.7) use a different task format. The instruction itself says "clone the repo `swesmith/<mirror>` and run `git fetch && git checkout <instance branch>`". Every one of those sandboxes holds the mirror's full history, including the clean `main`, by design. 8.8% of them then read git history.

**Method:** the shootout's own rules, used verbatim: `GIT_HISTORY_READ` from #202's selection, and the host prefix from chukar's `repository_pytest.py`. Each task's repo and fix lines come from DCAgent's packages (`78b0d879`). Code: [`scripts/task215/`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/29a6fb1919/scripts/task215); `audit.py` docstring and README list the exact regexes. Spot checks of random hits were all real history reads or real fix lines.

The shootout pool's fixed packages (one commit, no remote) and its no-internet agent phase close this path for new traces. Any SFT that used these sets' passes trained on traces that may have copied the fix.

topics.title: Agentic SFT shootout on Snowball v0: plain, RS-multi, relay, recovery, plateau dropping
topics.body:
## TL;DR

Design stage, 2026-10-16. We compare five supervised fine-tuning (SFT) mechanisms for agentic coding on one base, one task pool, one teacher and one supervised-token budget: plain SFT (one accepted demonstration per task), rejection-sampled SFT with resampling across epochs, relay SFT (#10027), recovery SFT, and plateau dropping (#10028). The earlier transfer experiments (#9920, #9984) compared plain SFT, rejection-sampled SFT, on-policy distillation and weight merging on non-agentic tasks; this experiment moves to agentic tasks under the eval policy (#10197) and drops merging and distillation. Nothing has trained yet except a learning-rate sweep of the control, which is in progress.

## Question

Which mechanism, if any, improves Snowball v0 on SWE-bench Verified and the terminal benchmarks over plain SFT at equal supervised tokens, without losing retention on GSM8K, BFCL-Parity and GPQA-Diamond.

## Fixed choices

- Base: Snowball v0 = `open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Merge-Campaign3-DARE-Linear-02-2026.10.12` @ `4eeb756b`. v0 carries a diluted DARE graft of the allkimi relay SFT, so relay's lift reads smaller than it would on a pre-graft checkpoint; this is accepted because the question is what improves the release.
- Task pool: about 2,200 TMax environments (`allenai/TMax-SFT-16.5K`, tasks.zip) and about 2,100 SWE-smith tasks sampled from the Harbor packages in `DCAgent/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s`, stratified by repository, SWE-bench Verified repositories removed, decontaminated through DataKit against SWE-bench Verified, Terminal-Bench 2.1 and TBLite 2.0. Selection is outcome-blind. SWE-smith packages receive a git-history strip before the agent phase (#10212).
- Harness per task family, matching the policy's scoring agent: TMax under Terminus-2, SWE-smith under mini-swe-agent 2.1.0, both in Harbor under the policy pins.
- Teacher: GLM 5.3 through the internal inference service, 8 attempts per task, verified by each task's tests. v0 is never sampled except in relay, where it starts each task and GLM continues after a trigger (format error, context budget, completion claim).
- Recipe, shared by every arm: the #9984 comparison-arm settings (AdamW, betas 0.9/0.999, weight decay 0, clip 1.0, router bias frozen, batch 16 at 32k context, constant learning rate, loss averaged over supervised tokens), 3 epochs, replay of general SFT data (`nemotron_sft_v3`, reasoning kept) at one quarter of the agentic budget. The learning rate comes from the sweep below.

## Arms and token matching

B is the supervised-token count of the plain arm: the first passing attempt per task with at least one pass, one trajectory per task. Every arm trains on B agentic tokens plus the same replay slice for the same number of optimizer steps.

- Plain SFT (control): as above.
- RS-multi: identical task slots to plain; when a task recurs in a later epoch, a different passing attempt is used. Measures demonstration diversity at a fixed budget.
- Relay (#10027): v0's own turns stay in context with no loss; GLM's turns are trained; passing episodes subsampled to B. Episodes with no teacher turn are dropped.
- Recovery (phase 2): the plain trajectories; 20% receive one or two synthetic failed turns re-rendered in v0's measured error styles plus the real harness error, inserted through the parser; injections carry no loss, so the budget equals B by construction. Waits on a validated injection generator.
- Plateau dropping (#10028, phase 2): the plain trajectories; tokens whose loss has plateaued lose gradient; matched on optimizer steps, with gradient-carrying tokens reported. Waits on the trainer.

Phase 1 is plain, RS-multi and relay.

## Evaluation

Every arm, including plain, runs the retention gate (GSM8K, BFCL-Parity, GPQA-Diamond) and the agentic endpoint (SWE-bench Verified, Terminal-Bench 2.1, TBLite 2.0) under the policy's trial counts and pins. An arm passes when it has no decisive loss against plain on the gate and a decisive win over plain on at least one agentic benchmark with no decisive loss on the others, where decisive is the policy's rule (gap above 1.96 times the combined task-level standard error, each scaled by 1/sqrt(0.9)). One policy run resolves gaps of roughly 4 to 5 points on SWE-bench Verified and 8 to 10 on the terminal benchmarks; unresolved arms are reported with intervals and not promoted. Passing arms, plain and v0 go to the 23-benchmark tournament.

## Learning-rate sweep of the control

Running now, on pilot data (existing Qwen3.6-27B TMax traces and Kimi-2.5 SWE-smith traces, history-reading trials removed), four runs from v0 at 3e-7, 1e-6, 3e-6 and 1e-5, 3 epochs, recipe otherwise fixed. Screens per run: held-out validation loss on 5% of tasks, GSM8K, BFCL-Parity, SWE-bench Verified random-100 and a 100-task TBLite subset. Decision rule, fixed in advance: among rates with no decisive retention loss against v0, the best equal-weight mean of the two agentic screens; ties to the smaller rate. The chosen rate is confirmed once on the real plain-arm data and then frozen for all arms.

## Budget

Core (sweep, generation, phase 1, tournament) about 3,700 to 4,000 H100-hours; phase 2 adds about 2,400, of which 1,700 is an optional 20-epoch plateau comparison. GLM generation runs on the internal service and sandbox CPU and is outside the GPU budget.

## Status and next steps

- Pilot dataset and learning-rate sweep: in progress.
- Task pool, decontamination and package fix: in progress.
- Harness bring-up, one-task dry runs, a 200-task-per-family pass-rate pilot and a relay dry run: in progress. The full 8-attempt generation waits on their results.
- Then: phase-1 training, first-stage evaluation, tournament for passers; phase 2 when its code exists.

Design notes and diagrams are kept in the maintainer's notes and will be attached as results land.

## Decision log

- 2026-10-15: scope cut to SFT only; merging and on-policy distillation dropped. Base set to Snowball v0.
- 2026-10-16: one harness per task family following the policy's scoring agents; GLM 5.3 as the single teacher with regenerated traces instead of reusing Kimi and Qwen traces; RS arm redefined as resampling across epochs after the token-budgeted variant was found to re-weight tasks; task eligibility defined by teacher success only; unfiltered-SFT control dropped; primary endpoint set to the agentic benchmarks with the tournament secondary; git-history leak found in the SWE-smith packages and a strip added to the pool build.

# Research

No shootout arm has trained on the new task pool; the learning-rate sweep, package repair, and harness pilots are still in progress. Two checks are essential before full generation: [#10212](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10212) documents a SWE-smith git-history leak, and [#10027](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10027) preserves relay turn flags but does not yet apply the teacher-only loss mask.

**Relevant code**
- [`launcher.py#L554-L564`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/experiments/sft/launcher.py#L554-L564) — chat SFT masks user turns.
- [`datasets.py#L477-L493`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/levanter/src/levanter/data/text/datasets.py#L477-L493) — assistant spans receive loss.

# Proposed Fix

1. Validate the repaired SWE-smith packages from #10212: no agent-visible history or branches, gold patch passes, and unpatched task fails. Freeze an outcome-blind, decontaminated task manifest and report excluded history-reading traces.
2. Finish one-task dry runs, the 200-task-per-family pass-rate pilots, and a relay dry run under the pinned harnesses. Verify that relay student turns have zero loss after rendering while teacher turns retain loss. Start eight-attempt GLM generation only after those checks pass.
3. Finish the learning-rate sweep and confirm its selected rate on real plain-arm data. Give plain and RS-multi identical task slots, subsample relay to B supervised agentic tokens, and match all three arms on B, one-quarter replay, and optimizer steps; publish the token counts, manifests, checkpoints, and run links.
4. Evaluate phase 1 under [#10197](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10197), publish task-level scores and uncertainty for the retention gate and three agentic endpoints, and send only passing arms to the tournament. Run recovery and plateau dropping after validating the injection mask and trainer; report inconclusive arms with intervals instead of promoting them.

🤖 Teacher generation bring-up: one-task dry runs

## TL;DR

GLM 5.3 now runs end to end in both harnesses (Harbor `016dd78b`, Daytona sandboxes, run from cw-us-east-02a):
- TMax under Terminus-2, with the 65,536 / 16,384 limits from the policy;
- SWE-smith under the mini-swe-agent 2.1.0 adapter, with a 32,768-token window.

**The adapter question is answered.** The mini-swe-agent adapter runs a raw SWE-smith Harbor package unchanged, and the dry-run trace fit inside 32k (largest prompt 13.4k tokens). One trace says nothing about the length distribution; the pilot will measure it.

**The GLM pass on SWE-smith read the fix from git history** (#10212). Before the SWE-smith pass-rate pilot, the packages need the history-stripped repair.

**The pilot has not started.** It waits on a capacity confirmation for the GLM service.

## Per trial

| | TMax `task_000000_5c5b0938` | SWE-smith `swesmith-00003` |
|---|---|---|
| Reward | 0 in the first run, 1 in a rerun | 1 in both runs |
| Model calls | 4 | 16 to 17 |
| Prompt tokens (total / largest) | 9.3k to 10.1k / 3.7k | 145k to 156k (about 93% prefix-cached) / 13.4k |
| Completion tokens (reasoning) | 5.1k to 6.2k (4.2k to 5.2k) | 3.4k to 3.6k (0.5k to 0.8k) |
| Model time | 39 s | 16 s |
| Trial wall time | 42 to 93 s (environment build 3 to 45 s) | 74 to 80 s (verifier 20 to 25 s) |

## Effective generation settings

Both clients send only `model` and `max_tokens=16384`, so GLM runs on the service defaults. GLM 5.3's template then renders `Reasoning Effort: Max`.

Every request is logged by an in-cluster proxy. The log records the settings as sent and the full reply, reasoning included. The proxy also serves `/tokenize` with the `zai-org/GLM-5.3` tokenizer, because the mini-swe-agent context limiter needs it and the relay does not provide it. Its token counts matched the service on every request.

## Transcripts

Both harnesses write Harbor ATIF trajectories:
- **Terminus-2:** each step's message is the JSON action, and the reasoning is in `reasoning_content`.
- **mini-swe-agent:** native `bash` tool calls with `{returncode, output}` observations, but the trajectory **drops GLM's reasoning**. Training rows are therefore rebuilt from the proxy log, which keeps it. That rebuild checks clean on both dry runs.

## What the agent can see

Measured with an oracle-agent probe during the agent phase:

| | TMax (converted) | SWE-smith (raw package) |
|---|---|---|
| `/tests` | absent | absent |
| `/solution` | absent | absent |
| Other task files | none | none |
| Git history | no repository | 944 branches, including `main` and the full history |

The SWE-smith dry-run pass used that history: it ran `git show 614b134:<file>`, then checked its edit against that file. Details are in #10212.

## Other findings

- **TMax is not in Harbor format** in `tasks.zip`. The pool converts it with TMax's own `convert_to_harbor.py` at `hamishivi/tmax@6d3d606c`, minus 181 environments with hidden verifier assets, giving 2,019 tasks.
- **The dry-run TMax task looks flawed.** It runs an OpenMP parallel loop over the outer LU loop with 4 threads, while the test expects the sequential determinant. The task failed once and passed once.

## Next

- **TMax pilot:** 200 tasks x 2 attempts, seed 20261016, drawn uniformly from 1,963 eligible tasks (the pool minus #202's held-out ids). Staged; starts when capacity is confirmed.
- **SWE-smith pilot:** 200 x 2, stratified by repository, on the history-stripped packages.
- **Relay dry run:** 20 tasks per family, with v0 served by the policy serving config. GLM takes over on these triggers:
  - format error: GLM writes one repair turn;
  - context budget at 0.75 of the window: GLM continues to the end;
  - completion claim: v0's reply is withheld and logged, and GLM continues to the end.

Run folders: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/sft-shootout/generation/dryrun/{tmax-dry1,tmax-dry2,swe-dry3,swe-dry4,visibility1}`

🤖 Pool P is frozen: 4,119 tasks, 206 held out, 0 contaminated.

topics.title: [post-training] Mix PivotRL pivots into broad RLVR for SWE and terminal gains
topics.body:
## TL;DR

Three matched mixed-domain RLVR runs from the Grug Datakit SFT (October 5) test whether a share of [PivotRL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.21383) pivots improves SWE-bench Verified and OpenThoughts-TBLite without hurting the other domains, and whether pivot selection matters: RLVR alone, RLVR with selected SWE and Terminal pivots at 20% of prompts, and RLVR with random SWE and Terminal turns at the same share. Two optional arms move the selected share to 10% and 30%. Every arm stops at 12 steps. Status: prerequisites done; a two-step smoke run of B is running.

## Hypothesis

Pivots that the SFT policy's own pass rates select (#9933), rewarded by #9933's deterministic verifiers, improve SWE-bench Verified and OpenThoughts-TBLite at 20% of prompts while broad holdout accuracy stays within noise. Random SWE and Terminal turns at the same share help less. Training pivots alone has been hard to stabilize; mixing them into broad RLVR keeps the rest of the policy anchored.

## Setup

- **Start:** [open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.10.05](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.10.05), a pure SFT checkpoint. #9933 measured its SWE and Terminal pass rates on this policy, so the selections apply unchanged, and the RLVR data is unseen.
- **RLVR data:** [Nemotron-RL-Ultra-RLVR1-Cleaned-v3](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Nemotron-RL-Ultra-RLVR1-Cleaned-v3-2026-09-30) (84,403 train / 94 validation rows; 24% single-step tool use, 14% instruction following, 9% code, 13% math, no SWE or Terminal rows). Any SWE or terminal change between arms is therefore attributable to the added turns.
- **Recipe:** the #9735 reference/KL arm (frozen reference, KL 0.01, sequence-mean loss, entropy 0.001, router replay), 512 prompts × 16 samples per step, at most 12 steps, the same seed in every arm. SFT starts in #9735 collapsed after 12 to 20 steps. Asynchronous rollouts with staleness up to 2, TIS correction, a 102,400-token request window with 49,152 tokens per turn, and thinking on, as #9933 measured the pivots' pass rates.
- **RLVR blend as trained:** 63,590 of RLVR1's rows. MarinSkyRL now runs every Nemotron Ultra row as a task session, and code generation, NeMo tool use, NVARC inductive and Lean sessions execute in a Docker task machine that Iris task pods cannot start, so every arm omits those four agents (about 20% of RLVR1, including #9735's code domain). Rows containing a blank text message, which task conversations reject, are dropped too (3,991 RLVR, 59 Terminal). Validation keeps 67 of RLVR1's 94 rows.
- **Pivot prompts:** the runtime drops earlier assistant turns' reasoning from pivot prompts, which #9933's pass-rate measurement kept.
- **Pivots:** #9933's long-format SWE and Terminal candidates, selected at λ = 0.65 (1 to 10 passes of 16) from the pooled K = 16 pass rates already measured on this policy (`users/dml/pivotrl/{swe,terminal}/pass-rates/grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft-262k-20261005+seed-1@2026.10.09`). That selects 25,792 of 72,434 scored SWE turns under `nemo` and 6,999 of 36,107 Terminal turns.
- **Reward:** `nemotron_ultra` grades pivot rows through MarinSkyRL#992 with #9933's verifiers: NeMo Gym argument comparison (`nemo`) for SWE and Terminus-2 keystroke similarity without a judge (`string_90`) for Terminal. #10000 uses the same graders. Pivot replies are capped at 4,096 tokens, the cap the pass rates were sampled at.

## Arms

| Arm | Data |
| --- | --- |
| A | RLVR1 |
| B | RLVR1, with selected pivots replacing 20% of prompts |
| C | RLVR1, with random SWE and Terminal candidate turns replacing 20% of prompts |
| B-10, B-30 (optional) | As B, at 10% and 30% |

The batch stays at 512 prompts, so added turns displace RLVR prompts. Each step carries 102 added turns, 51 SWE and 51 Terminal, because the two benchmarks weigh equally in the decision rules; MarinSkyRL's domain-weighted sampling fills every batch to these counts from route-tagged pools and draws each pool uniformly. RLVR rows come first and their pool is shuffled first, so with one seed B's and C's RLVR prompts are a prefix of A's draw order. Twelve steps use 612 of each pool (25,792 SWE and 6,999 Terminal pivots), so no turn repeats.

### Why 20%

Only groups with mixed outcomes produce a gradient, and RLVR1 groups already mostly do: `reward/informative_group_fraction` was 0.79 at the first step from the Datakit SFT (Datakit v4, #9735) and fell to about 0.55 by step 12. Resampling the stored K = 16 pass rates, 88% of selected SWE pivots and 81% of selected Terminal pivots come back mixed, against 58% and 24% of random candidate turns. Pivots' share of the gradient is therefore only 1.1 to 1.5 times their share of prompts, and C carries about half of B's pivot signal at the same share.

Pivot-only RL on this SFT, with the same policy learning rate (4e-6) and gradient clip, bounds the dose. One update of 64 SWE pivot groups raised SWE-bench Verified from 26.0% to 29.4% (146 vs 129 of 496 matched tasks, against a historical base run) with AIME24 unchanged; five updates raised held-out pivot accuracy from 0.29 to 0.38. Forty Terminal updates cost 36 points on AIME24 and 9 to 10 on GPQA Diamond, MMLU-Pro and Math500, and ninety SWE updates collapsed agentic behavior (1 of 248 SWE-bench Verified trials solved, 0 of 190 TBLite) while held-out pivot accuracy kept rising.

Counting a mixed step as its pivot gradient share of a pivot-only update, with RLVR1's informative fraction averaging about 0.68 over the first 12 steps, a first-order approximation that ignores RLVR and KL counteracting drift:

| *p* | Pivot prompts per step | Pivot gradient share | Equivalent pivot-only updates by step 12 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 10% | 51 | ~12% | ~1.5 |
| 20% | 102 | ~24% | ~2.9 |
| 30% | 154 | ~35% | ~4.2 |

With at most 12 steps, 10% delivers about one pivot-only update, the dose that gained about 3 points on SWE, below what the benchmarks resolve. 20% places the dose in the middle of the range where pivot-only training helped, about 14 times below where it did damage, with RLVR still about three quarters of the gradient. B-10 and B-30 bracket it.

## Measurements

- At steps 0, 4, 8 and 12: pass rate on #9933's held-out validation turns graded in process, broad holdout pass@1 and normalized verifier score, and per-domain reward.
- Per step and per source (RLVR, SWE, Terminal): informative group count and mean response length, so B and C are compared by delivered pivot signal and any pull toward shorter RLVR answers shows up early. Pivot replies are capped at 4,096 tokens, the cap their pass rates were sampled at, through each pivot row's request; the sequence-mean loss weights them like full RLVR answers.
- At step 0 and each arm's step 4, 8 and 12 checkpoints: full SWE-bench Verified (500 tasks, mini-swe-agent 2.1.0) and OpenThoughts-TBLite (Terminus 2), three runs each, compared per task between arms, plus AIME24, GPQA Diamond, MMLU-Pro and Math500, the benchmarks pivot-only training hurt.
- Checkpoints are selected by the broad holdout and pivot validation, never by the benchmarks. A paired comparison on 500 SWE tasks has a standard error of about 2 points; on 100 tasks it is about 4.4, too wide for the effects expected here.

## Decision rules

- B beats A on SWE-bench Verified or OpenThoughts-TBLite by more than two paired standard errors, with the broad holdout and the four reasoning benchmarks within noise: pivots help in mixed RLVR. Next, test RL-then-merge against the Campaign 3 merge recipe (#9975).
- B ≈ C: selection does not matter at this share; random turns are enough. B > C partly reflects C's smaller pivot signal, so the logged informative group counts qualify the comparison.
- B beats A on pivot validation only: the verifier reward does not transfer to the benchmarks. Revisit the reward component (`exact`) or the generation cap.
- An arm collapses: report its best checkpoint before the collapse and compare arms only at matched steps.

## Prerequisites

1. Per-agent `pivot_reward`, declared among the Nemotron Ultra session settings: MarinSkyRL#992.
2. Selection artifacts at λ = 0.65 from #9933's stored K = 16 pass rates: built, 25,792 SWE and 6,999 Terminal pivots.
3. Arm datasets: #10215 builds RLVR1 (`open-athena/Nemotron-RL-Ultra-RLVR1-Cleaned-v3-2026-09-30@600262dd`) alone, with the selected pivots, and with every scored candidate turn, each row tagged with its route. Rows move from the retired `skyrl_gym` route to `task_session`, which MarinSkyRL grades Nemotron Ultra rows on since its #879. Validation in every arm is RLVR1's 94 rows plus #9933's 508 held-out SWE and 503 Terminal turns.
4. A two-step smoke run of B on 6 nodes (64 prompts with B's composition, 32K window) confirming that every agent's rows load and grade.

## Links

- PivotRL candidates, pass rates and selection: #9933; SFT baselines on the same pivots: #10000; TaskSpec versions of the candidates: #10181
- Prior broad-domain RLVR: #9359, #9735
- Paper: [PivotRL (arXiv 2603.21383)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.21383)

topics.title: [finestore] Merge sorted runs and resolve versions in Arrow
topics.body:
FineStore compaction, scans, and `iter_rows` now resolve primary-key versions in Arrow instead of row by row in Python. Compaction becomes a sorted-run merge whose output shards hold disjoint, ascending key ranges.

Compaction used to order input row groups by their first key, keep the newest version of every key in a Python dictionary one row at a time, and then hand each output row to the shard writer as its own slice. `scan` and `iter_rows` also compared versions per row in Python. Version resolution therefore dominated compaction time, and a key could recur across one compaction's output shards.

`finestore.merge` selects the newest row per key with one Arrow sort and a key-change mask, using the existing order: a greater `(_commit, _seq, _gen)` wins, a missing `_seq` counts as zero, and null keys sort last and compare equal. A key column that no row sets is null for every row. `merge_sorted_runs` keeps a sorted buffer per run and merges by a frontier: buffered rows below the smallest last key among the runs are final and are sorted once as they leave, and only the runs at the frontier read their next table. Memory holds about one table per run.

Compaction reads each sorted input a row group at a time. An unsorted input, such as a flush with a row missing a key column or a shard migrated from format 1, is sorted whole in memory, so a compaction holds all of its unsorted inputs at once; these are expected to be rare. Output shards are cut at about `target_bytes`. `iter_rows` streams the same merge, and `scan` uses the vectorised selection while keeping its row order; `scan` also resolves versions when a key column is absent, as `iter_rows` does.

Local root, 16 overlapping level-zero shards of 20,000 rows each (320,000 rows, 95,874 live keys), against main on the same machine:

| | main | this change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `compact_table`, 1,024-row row groups | 51.7 s, 79 MB Arrow peak, 33 MB Python peak | 0.9 s, 4.7 MB, 0.4 MB |
| `compact_table`, default row groups | 43.6 s | 0.15 s |
| `scan` | 0.78 s | 0.11 s |
| `iter_rows` | 1.69 s | 0.5 s |

Object-store traffic is unaffected: the 16-writer simulated S3 benchmark issued 1,772 requests, against 1,789 on main.

This is the merge half of P2 in the FineStore concurrency proposal (Loom session bth4qn4d, artifact `finestore-improvements`). The proposed `_version` column is not added: while every commit goes through one `HEAD`, `(_commit, _seq, _gen)` is already a total order, and `_version` only becomes necessary with per-writer heads (P3), so it should land with that format change.

🤖 Code review

No issues found.

<!-- marin-correctness-review -->

🤖 Holistic review of 4fddb8ab9d4371931e3c467731bbea1e2a1a24d0.

This change moves FineStore's newest-version selection from per-row Python into Arrow and turns compaction into a sorted-run merge. Reads and compaction now share one module, `finestore/merge.py`. Since the last review, the merge keeps a separate buffer for each run and no longer re-sorts carried rows. One problem remains: compaction holds every unsorted input shard fully in memory at the same time.

**Before.** Compaction ordered input row groups by their first key through `heapq.merge`, kept the newest version of each key in a Python dict, and flushed that buffer as a sorted output shard each time it passed `target_bytes` (the bound added in #10188). Keys could appear in more than one output shard. `iter_rows` merged per-shard Python row streams, and `scan`'s `_deduplicate` sorted indices in Python.

**Design.** `newest_indices` sorts by key ascending (nulls last), then by `(_commit, _seq→0, _gen)` descending, and keeps the first row of each key using a key-change mask. A key column that is absent or null-typed is skipped, since it is null in every row. `merge_sorted_runs` keeps a `_RunCursor` buffer for each run with contiguous key arrays. Each round takes the buffered rows below the smallest `last_key` among the active runs, resolves versions on only those rows, and pulls the next table only for runs at that frontier. Before a pull, leftover versions of the frontier key shrink to one row. Compaction feeds `_sorted_run(shard)` into the merge, then into `table_row_groups`, and cuts output shards near `target_bytes`. Its output shards cover disjoint key ranges.

**Evidence and limits.** The 249 finestore tests pass locally at this head. They include a randomized merge-vs-dict oracle (40 seeds) and compaction tests for disjoint output ranges, an unsorted flush, and a key column that no row sets. That last test reproduces Codex's `ArrowInvalid` report. My microbenchmark of `merge_sorted_runs` (2M int keys, one run as a single table, the other in 1,024-row tables) took 7.2 s at 57ae77bc and takes 0.13 s now. I did not reproduce the benchmark table in the PR body.

**Findings**

- **1. Should fix (open):** `lib/finestore/src/finestore/compaction.py:223` still holds every unsorted input shard in memory at once. `_RunCursor.__init__` calls `pull()` (`merge.py:111`), so constructing the merge reads the first table of every run. For an unsorted shard that table is the whole shard, because `sorted_by_key` (`merge.py:49`) runs `list(tables)` over it. Peak memory is therefore the decoded size of all unsorted inputs together, where #10188 bounded it to about `target_bytes`. Every shard migrated from format v1 is unsorted (`migrations/m0001_manifest.py:249` builds `Shard(...)` without `primary_key_sorted`), and `compact_table` has no input budget. An explicit or leveled compaction of a migrated archive would therefore decode every legacy shard into memory together. Sort unsorted inputs one at a time before the merge, for example by rewriting each into a sorted temporary run, so peak memory is one shard. Add a test that compacts two unsorted shards and checks they are not materialized together. (`iter_rows` already buffered unsorted shards this way before this PR, so the regression is limited to compaction.)

Earlier findings: 2 resolved in 4fddb8ab; per-run buffers sort only rows that have become final, so a whole-shard run no longer gets re-sorted every round.

<!-- marin-holistic-review:4fddb8ab9d4371931e3c467731bbea1e2a1a24d0 -->

🤖 Removed the merge module's caller list and the compaction docstring's hard byte-limit claim in 5769d365e5. Pre-commit and 208 FineStore tests passed. The review's two behavior-changing findings remain with the PR author.

<!-- marin-deslop:57ae77bc6088cecf11a3365efa7580ef6957d9ca -->

🤖 Both findings are addressed.

1. Unsorted inputs are no longer held together (2f9e4d331e). Before the merge, each unsorted shard is read a row group at a time into chunks of at most `target_bytes` decoded bytes. Each chunk is sorted and written to a local temporary Parquet file, which the merge reads as another sorted run. `test_compaction_sorts_unsorted_shards_one_at_a_time` compacts 2 and then 6 unsorted 8 MiB shards. Peak Arrow memory is 25 MB in both cases, where the previous code grew from 56 MB to 152 MB and fails the test.
2. The carried remainder is no longer re-sorted each round (4fddb8ab9d, also Codex's finding). Each run keeps its own sorted buffer, a round binary-searches every buffer for the rows below the frontier, and only those rows are sorted. One 400,000-row run against 400 tables of 1,000 rows now merges in 0.36 s, down from 2.2 s. Slicing the sorted table is unnecessary with buffers, because a large buffer costs one binary search per round.

🤖 Reverted the spill in c62881fb6a. Unsorted inputs come only from flushes with a row missing a key column and from shards migrated from format 1, which may no longer exist. Temporary-file handling isn't worth carrying for that case. A compaction again sorts its unsorted inputs in memory and holds them together, and the README now says so.

topics.title: [grug] Read precomputed fa4_bounds in the AMD Pallas flash kernel
topics.body:
`moe_hero_ep`, `moe_hero_fsdp` and `fast_track` run their layers in one homogeneous `lax.scan` and pick each layer's sliding window by selecting between precomputed `fa4_bounds` arrays (`experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py:1339-1359`). They have to: the window is a static `AttentionMask` field that the scan body cannot vary. `gpu_pallas_triton_flash` rejected any mask that carried those bounds, so none of these models could run on AMD GPUs with it. The kernel now uses the bounds as its per-query key lower bounds, as `gpu_fa4_cute` does.

A padding query (`valid=False`) attends only to itself, so outputs differ from the segment-ID path only on padding rows, which the loss masks. The new test runs the kernel with the bounds and with the equivalent segment-ID mask, full causal and window 40, and requires outputs on document rows and all gradients to agree to 1e-6.

topics.title: [evaluation] Resume brokered evals and expose serving status
topics.body:
Await inference responses asynchronously so the proxy’s outstanding-request limit is not capped by AnyIO’s 40-thread pool. Expose an HTML status page at `/status` with queue counts, dispatch delay, worker registration, response errors, and proxy timeouts and rejections. Report prompt, output, and total tokens from completed responses, with 60-second and lifetime rates and response usage coverage.

Run multiple serving instances behind one broker with `--instances` and bound simultaneous evaluator jobs with `--max-concurrent`. Evaluation serving workers allow 64 concurrent HTTP requests each; proxy capacity is `max(256, 64 * instances)`, including requests already running. GPU evals use a 4,096-token scheduling budget and TPU evals retain 512, with model-level overrides.

Make `launch --run-id` reuse evaluation identities and existing output archives. Concurrency changes preserve identity; model, scoring, and evaluator-runtime changes produce distinct step IDs and output archives under the same run ID. Adopt Evalchemy cf5c040, which permits inference endpoint and concurrency changes during partial recovery while preserving model, generation, code, and dependency checks.

Read aggregate scores from Evalchemy’s result table, retain evaluator-owned benchmark metadata, and derive rollouts from normalized samples without changing the samples table’s conflict policy. Missing or unscored task results fail the affected eval. Set broker worker, lease, and proxy deadlines 60, 120, and 180 seconds beyond the evaluator’s 30-minute budget, and allow 40 minutes for serving startup.
topics.head: 91f7060944327c3f03070728f4d8196be69a0ae8

comments.body:
🤖 Holistic review of b37c75fd8f64008e3c3beea691e33b3c7bf6e26c.

This PR lets one evaluation launch run N candidate serving instances behind a shared request broker, moves Marin onto Evalchemy's FineStore result table (pin now `cf5c040`), and adds a resumable `--run-id` launch plus a `/status` page on the broker proxy. Earlier findings 1 and 2 are resolved. One identity inconsistency remains open, along with three related-PR notes.

**Serving.** Before this PR, the evaluation path always passed one instance, and a brokered launch would have used iris's default `BrokerConfig()` deadlines (180 s worker, 300 s proxy). Now, when `instances > 1` and no broker is given, `inference_config_for_model` (`serving_config.py:251`) derives every deadline from `EVALCHEMY_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 1800`, which `evalchemy/client.py` exports. The worker deadline is that budget plus 60 s, the lease plus 120 s, and the proxy plus 180 s. Each worker allows 64 in-flight requests, and the proxy allows `max(256, 64 * instances)` pending requests. `InferenceProxy.forward_raw_request` is now `async`. It still submits through `anyio.to_thread`, but it waits on the response with `asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.shield(asyncio.wrap_future(future)))` (`proxy.py:249`). A request waiting on inference therefore no longer holds one of AnyIO's 40 worker threads. The new proxy test drives 64 concurrent requests through the ASGI app to cover this. `InferenceBroker.status()` returns a `BrokerStatus` with queue counts, lease counts, response counts, and queue-wait figures. Through the actor handle that `_start_brokered_inference` casts to `InferenceResponseProvider`, `/status` renders that snapshot as escaped HTML.

**Results.** `read_evalchemy_results` (`lm_eval_samples.py:791`) now fails in two cases: a configured task prefix has no `evalchemy_results` row, or a row has `scored=False`. Callers pass the expected prefixes from `eval_task_directory`. `BenchmarkMetadataRef` switches to `extra="allow"`, so evaluator-owned metadata such as source, reducers, and prompt length survives into the record.

**Resume.** Before this PR, a CLI launch drew a fresh `uuid4` run ID for each eval, so a relaunch could not reuse anything. Now `group_id = spec.run_id or _group_id(...)`. Each eval's run ID is `uuid5` over a JSON identity that includes the run ID. On the CLI path, that identity excludes `serve.{max_num_batched_tokens,max_num_seqs,gpu_memory_utilization}`, `source_digest`, and `evalchemy.num_concurrent`. Relaunching with the same `--run-id` and records prefix therefore lets `StepRunner` skip completed evals and reuse the partial FineStore archives. Evalchemy `cf5c040` accepts the changed endpoint and concurrency during partial recovery. `test_launch.py` covers both outcomes through the real CLI: a relaunch with changed concurrency keeps each eval's identity, and a change of model or limit gets new ones.

**Evidence.** At this head, I ran `test_launch.py`, `test_inference_proxy.py`, `test_evaluation.py`, and `test_eval_archive.py` locally: 154 passed. Nothing exercises brokered serving or Evalchemy partial recovery on a cluster. topics.title: mini-swe-agent sandbox contains clean copies of SWE-smith task repositories
topics.body:
When Harbor runs the mini-swe-agent 2.1.0 adapter on a SWE-smith task, the agent's own Python environment is installed inside the task sandbox at agent setup (`/root/.local/share/uv/tools/mini-swe-agent/lib/python3.12/site-packages/`). That environment contains clean, unbroken copies of three packages that are also SWE-smith task repositories: pygments, pandas and tenacity. The agent can read the fixed source directly. The same class exists at the image level, independent of the agent: conda's package cache ships boltons in every conda image, pip and setuptools vendor chardet, tomli and inflect, and one testbed environment holds an installed dataset egg.

Observed: in a GLM 5.3 trial on `swesmith-00763` (jd/tenacity) with the mini-swe-agent adapter, the agent ran `sed -n 136,175p /root/.local/share/uv/tools/mini-swe-agent/lib/python3.12/site-packages/tenacity/retry.py`, called it "the reference", copied the logic and passed. A pre-agent audit of the task packages cannot see this environment, because it appears only when the agent is installed.

Scope in the DCAgent SWE-smith packages (`DCAgent/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s`), measured with mini-swe-agent's dependencies pinned (identical 80 distributions across one image per repository): pygments 222 tasks, pandas 196, tenacity 30, boltons 21, chardet 10, tomli 23, inflect 27, dataset 13. In the 2,100-task shootout pool that was 542 tasks before replacement. A filename-only check produces false positives (pygments' `html.py` versus safety, IPython's `timing.py` versus alive-progress), so the check must compare module contents or names, not file suffixes.

Reproduce: start a trial with the mini-swe-agent adapter on any pygments, pandas or tenacity SWE-smith task, and in the agent phase list `/root/.local/share/uv/tools/mini-swe-agent/lib/python3.12/site-packages/<package>/`. For the image-level copies, build the task's `environment/Dockerfile` and search outside `/testbed` for directories named after the task repository's import name (for example `find / -path /testbed -prune -o -type d -name tomli -print`).

Impact: pass rates on those tasks are inflated and the resulting traces teach reading a library copy instead of fixing the bug. Terminus-2 is not affected by the tool-environment copy, because the Terminus-2 agent runs outside the sandbox, but the image-level copies affect every agent. Existing SWE-smith trace sets were generated with other agent setups, so their tool environments may differ; they have not been audited for these paths.

Expected: during the agent phase, no readable copy of the task repository exists outside `/testbed`. Either the agent environment lives outside the sandbox (as Terminus-2 does), or the adapter installs it on a path the agent cannot read, or task packages whose repository is a dependency of the agent or of the base image are excluded from training pools and flagged in evaluation.

Done when: Harbor's mini-swe-agent adapter keeps its environment out of the agent's reach or documents the limitation; a content-based image check for repository copies outside `/testbed` is part of SWE-smith package validation; and existing SWE-smith trace sets are audited for reads under these paths. The shootout pool (#10213) already excludes the eight repositories above, pins the agent's dependencies, and drops traces that read a library copy of the task repository; the method and per-repository evidence are in the pool manifest at `open-athena/Snowball-SFT-Shootout-Pool-2026.10`. Related: #10212 (git history left in the same packages).

comments.body:
🤖

# Research

Harbor's Mini-SWE setup puts its Python tool environment inside the task container; a GLM 5.3 trial read the installed `tenacity/retry.py` and passed using that reference ([probe](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10212#issuecomment-6227834962)). [Pool P v4](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10213#issuecomment-6228022768) excludes the affected repositories, and its row builder drops known library-copy reads, but those controls apply to this shootout rather than to future SWE-smith packages or older traces. Marin delegates agent execution to the pinned Harbor runtime, so the adapter, package validator, and trace audit need separate changes.

**Relevant code**
- [`trial_driver.py#L104-L116`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/trial_driver.py#L104-L116) — Harbor agent selection.
- [`driver_config.py#L69-L80`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/driver_config.py#L69-L80) — pinned external runtime.
- [`penfever_rollouts.py#L702-L708`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/penfever_rollouts.py#L702-L708) — one historical SWE-smith trace source.

# Proposal

Keep the v4 exclusions as the current safeguard. Add the following durable checks before treating other SWE-smith packages or historical traces as clean.

1. **Harbor adapter:** Move the Mini-SWE controller and its Python environment outside the task sandbox; send tool commands through Harbor's sandbox execution interface. Probe after agent setup, when the tool environment currently appears, and verify that the agent can edit `/testbed` but cannot read the controller's packages. If Harbor cannot support this boundary, document the limitation in the adapter and reject repository/agent pairs whose code ships in its pinned dependencies. The adapter change belongs in `marin-community/harbor`; Marin should pin the tested revision.
2. **Package validation:** Promote the [v4 image probe](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10212#issuecomment-6228022644) into the SWE-smith package build gate. Inspect agent-readable files outside `/testbed` in the built image and again after agent setup. Use repository import names and distribution metadata to find candidates, then confirm source overlap with content fingerprints; a matching filename alone must not reject a task. Record matched paths, files, image revision, and agent dependency pin in the manifest, and reject confirmed overlaps before publishing packages.
3. **Historical traces:** Inventory each existing SWE-smith trace source and its agent/setup revision, starting with the registered Penfever source and the Kimi traces noted in [#10212](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10212#issuecomment-6228022644). Join commands and observations to the task repository; flag reads from its copies in `site-packages`, `_vendor`, conda caches, eggs, Go module caches, and agent tool environments. Publish counts and example paths by dataset and repository, quarantine confirmed contaminated rows, and mark sources with missing command or environment provenance as unknown rather than clean. Run the audit where the traces are stored to avoid bulk cross-region transfer.

## Testing and rollout

Test the validator against the observed tenacity tool environment and vendored tomli, plus unrelated files such as Pygments' `html.py`; the latter must not trigger on its filename. Run one Mini-SWE task end to end with the new boundary and verify that setup, editing, and the verifier still work. Hand-check flagged and unflagged audit samples, publish the audit manifest and rejected counts, then require the validator result in future SWE-smith pool manifests.

## Costs and open question

Moving the controller changes Harbor's agent lifecycle and needs an integration test, while scanning built images adds package-build work. Can Harbor's current Mini-SWE adapter run outside the sandbox with its existing command transport? If not, the documented limitation plus enforced repository exclusions is the immediate adapter deliverable; the package gate and trace audit remain required.

🤖 **TL;DR:** in the existing SWE-smith trace sets, clean copies outside `/testbed` matter little for the testbed-format tasks, and mini-swe-agent's tool env never appears. They ran Terminus-2, not mini-swe-agent. The exception is AgentTrove's clone-format tasks: 1,142 of their traces read an installed release copy of the task's own package.

| Set (revision) | Traces | Agent command reads a library copy of the task's repo | Touches mini-swe-agent's tool env | Row-builder drop (copy or tool env anywhere in the trace) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `open-athena/Kimi-2.5-swesmith-...-maxeps-32k` (`1b87a9cf78`) | 9,356 | 2 (1 of 5,237 passes) | 0 | 6 |
| `laion/calibforge-relay-traces` `kimi_swesmith` (`66feab4d24`) | 4,392 | 1 (0 passes) | 0 | 3 |
| `DCAgent2/GLM-4.7-swesmith-...-maxeps-131k` (`e209a88db1`) | 9,437 | 3 | 0 | 10 |
| `open-thoughts/AgentTrove` swesmith rows (`b395a4307a`) | 78,246 | 1,157 (1,142 in clone tasks) | 0 | 1,598 |

- **Clone tasks:** the instruction makes the agent clone `swesmith/<mirror>` into an image that already has the package installed. The agents then `ls` or `cat` the installed copy (`/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/<pkg>`, `/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/<pkg>`, a venv's `site-packages`), and that copy is clean code. 106 repos are affected; cantools, pygments, oauthlib and python-docx lead. The same tasks also expose the full mirror history (see #10212).
- **Go module cache:** 2 traces read a Go repo's module-cache copy. The shootout lists no import names for Go repos, so this column is supplementary.

**Method:** the shootout row builder's own rules, used verbatim: `LIBRARY_LOCATION` plus the repo's import names, and `AGENT_TOOL_ENV`. They are applied to the agent's commands, and also to the whole trace, matching the builder's drop rule. Import names are the shootout's for its 38 repos and extended for the rest. Code and exact regexes: [`scripts/task215/`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/29a6fb1919/scripts/task215).
