topics.title: [taskcompendium] Merge output_paths, collect, and artifacts into one capture
topics.body:
The rollout engine must keep the task machine, and the agent that used it, alive until grading ends. The engine copies `TaskSpec.output_paths` from the task machine, then passes the live machine to `grade_in_sandbox`. For a `ScriptGrader`, `grade_in_sandbox` runs the `collect` commands on that machine and copies the `artifacts` out before it starts the verifier machine (`lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/runtime/grading.py:512`, `:528`, `:545`). Thus the engine cannot close the task machine while the verifier runs, and an agent that is still running can change files before the grader copies them.

Three fields say what to take from the task machine. Each has a different owner, limit, and destination:

- `TaskSpec.output_paths`: files returned in `Rollout.outputs` and given to every grader at the same paths. The limit is 1,024 files and 16 MiB in total, because the rollout holds them in memory.
- `ScriptGrader.collect`: commands that run as root on the task machine to make grader inputs. Only the SWE importer uses them, to write the agent's change as a patch (`lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/importers/swe.py:51`).
- `ScriptGrader.artifacts`: files or directories copied into the verifier machine only. The limit is 1 GiB and 100,000 files. Users: the SWE patch, the whole workspace of the tasktrove repository-build tasks (`experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/tasktrove/repository_build.py:105`), and `/testbed` in the Harbor tests (`experiments/post_training/task_curation/tests/test_harbor.py:632`).

Proposed: replace the three fields with one task-level capture that the engine runs once, after the harness ends.

```python
class CapturePath(BaseModel):
    path: str                       # a file or a directory on the task machine
    exclude: tuple[str, ...] = ()   # patterns to skip inside a directory
    required: bool = False          # True: a missing path fails the capture


class Capture(BaseModel):
    commands: tuple[VerifierCommand, ...] = ()  # run first, as root, on the task machine
    paths: tuple[CapturePath, ...] = ()
```

The capture writes each path into one local directory, at its original location. The rollout points to that directory, and every grader reads only from it. An in-process grader reads the files, and a script grader's verifier machine gets them at the same paths. The engine can then close the task machine and stop the agent while grading runs, and wait for both at the end. A failed close or stop stays a cleanup error and does not change the grade. Captures are on disk at every size, so small files and large directories need no separate fields. State that is not a file must be written to a file by a capture command, for example with `pg_dump` or `curl localhost:8080 > response.txt`.

To decide:

- Who deletes the capture directory. A proposal: `run_task` deletes it after grading, unless the caller asks to keep it to grade again later. The caller of a rollout without grading owns it.
- The size limit. Today's artifact limit (1 GiB, 100,000 files) is a starting point.
- The TaskCompendium grading API in two steps, `capture(task, machine)` and `grade(task, attempt, captured)`, which the curation pipelines (`grade_task`) also use.

Related: #9763 and #9978 ask to grade a supplied final state without model inference. With the two-step API, that is `grade(task, attempt, captured)`, where the captured directory comes from a builder or from the capture of a prepared machine. This came up in the harness redesign of #10203.

Done when:

- `TaskSpec` has one capture field, and `output_paths`, `ScriptGrader.collect`, and `ScriptGrader.artifacts` are removed, with a new schema version.
- No grader receives the task machine: `grade_in_sandbox` reads the captured directory.
- The engine closes the task machine and stops the agent while it grades, and a failed close or stop is a cleanup error.
- The SWE importer, the tasktrove repository-build tasks, and every `output_paths` user are migrated, and their tests pass.

comments.body:
🤖

# Research

The engine captures `output_paths` after the turn loop, but `grade_in_sandbox` runs `ScriptGrader.collect` and copies `artifacts` later, while it still holds the task machine. The attempt's resource stack closes the episode and task machine after grading, so the verifier is coupled to a live, mutable workspace. The existing output capture is limited to 1,024 files/16 MiB in memory; artifact transfer uses a separate tar path with a 1 GiB/100,000-member limit.

**Relevant code**
- [`models.py#L580-L614`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5b622ba264e0a9329a26b29422f96dcf1dafe1c4/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/models.py#L580-L614) — grader-owned collection fields
- [`output_capture.py#L14-L54`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5b622ba264e0a9329a26b29422f96dcf1dafe1c4/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/runtime/output_capture.py#L14-L54) — in-memory output limit
- [`grading.py#L499-L558`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5b622ba264e0a9329a26b29422f96dcf1dafe1c4/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/runtime/grading.py#L499-L558) — live-machine collection during grading
- [`engine.py#L392-L414`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5b622ba264e0a9329a26b29422f96dcf1dafe1c4/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/engine.py#L392-L414) — capture and grade order
- [`harbor_export.py#L210-L235`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5b622ba264e0a9329a26b29422f96dcf1dafe1c4/experiments/post_training/task_curation/tasktrove/harbor_export.py#L210-L235) — repository artifact assumption

# Design: one task capture

## Goal

Each attempt should make one bounded, local snapshot of the task machine after the agent finishes. Grading, including repeat grading of a supplied final state, should use that snapshot without receiving the task machine. This is a design-level change across TaskCompendium, RolloutEngine, curation, and task authors; it needs a dedicated implementation PR after the harness contract in [#10203](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10203) settles. No open PR targets #10225; [#9838](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9838) covers the related supplied-state path and should be reconciled with the new capture API.

## Design and implementation order

1. Add `TaskSpec.capture: Capture` with ordered `commands` and `CapturePath(path, exclude, required)`, then remove `TaskSpec.output_paths`, `ScriptGrader.collect`, and `ScriptGrader.artifacts`. Bump `SCHEMA_VERSION` from 0.27 and reject old serialized tasks. Validate normalized absolute paths, reject overlaps with private verifier roots and overlapping capture roots, and keep the original absolute path as the grader destination. Commands run in order as root after the episode is quiescent.
2. Make `capture(task, machine)` produce an owned local directory, with files and empty directories laid out relative to `/`. Reuse the artifact tar extraction's link/path checks and preserve modes and timestamps. Enforce one aggregate 1 GiB/100,000-member budget across all paths; an optional missing path is omitted, a required missing path or unsafe member is a submission failure, and command or machine failure remains an infrastructure error. Capture once, then read only the local directory. A direct `grade(task, attempt, captured)` entry point and the curation `grade_task` wrapper should share the same grader dispatch; neither receives `Machine`.
3. Port the engine onto #10203's `run_task`/harness surface. End the episode's ability to write to the task machine and wait for its agent to stop **before** capture, including on turn-limit and timeout paths; copying while an agent can still write would leave the race in place. After capture, start task-machine cleanup while grading reads the local directory, then await cleanup before returning. Keep close/stop failures in `cleanup_errors` without changing a completed grade. Change harness grading so a `SessionGrader` reads the immutable rollout and capture, not a live episode or machine.
4. Define ownership so `run_task` removes the directory after grading by default and returns no dangling path; an explicit retain option transfers cleanup to the caller. A rollout that runs without grading transfers ownership to its caller. The returned rollout can name a capture directory only when it is retained. Keep `GradingAttempt.state` for caller-supplied JSON state; machine state needed by a grader must be written to a captured file by a command.
5. Migrate the SWE patch command, tasktrove repository-build workspace, ARC and tasktrove `output_paths` constructors, Harbor export, curation controls and audit projections, `direct_chat`, serialized fixtures, and rollout documentation. Regenerate persisted TaskSpec rows at the new schema version. Coordinate with [#9784](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9784), whose open Taskforge spec builder still names `output_paths`, and adapt #9838's prepared-state flow to call the same capture and grade functions.

## Validation

Test missing and excluded paths, aggregate budgets, links and path traversal, file modes, and an empty directory. An end-to-end attempt should prove that changing or closing the task machine after capture cannot change the grade, and that close failures preserve the grade while appearing in cleanup diagnostics. Exercise SWE patch grading, tasktrove repository grading, curation's supplied-state path, and the Harbor export contract. Run the TaskCompendium and RolloutEngine suites, affected curation tests, type checking, and the repository pre-commit gates before a PR.

## Open question

The proposed 1 GiB/100,000-member budget is global, unlike today's per-artifact check. Measure a representative tasktrove repository capture before fixing that limit; if it exceeds the budget, put an explicit larger cap in the task capture contract rather than silently truncating it.

topics.title: [finestore] Prefetch small compaction inputs concurrently
topics.body:
FineStore compactions with at most 16 MiB of compressed input now fetch whole shards with up to 16 concurrent reads and reuse those bytes for schema and row reads. Larger compactions keep their bounded streaming reads.

[A live evaluation](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fpower%2Feval-20261017-015918-qwen3-8b-59475eeeb8a94886a01e373e84d3f073-3066d84b%2Feval-drop-5c76ab07) took 9.83 seconds to compact 17 shards containing 128 rows and 196 KB. Its isolated Evalchemy environment was already running `marin-finestore 0.2.197.dev38989978700`, including #10209 and #10216. Compaction still reopened shards for schema, footer, and data reads, issuing those reads serially.

In a synthetic benchmark with 17 small shards and 100 ms per simulated S3 request, total compaction time falls from 5.76 to 0.85 seconds and GETs fall from 54 to 20. A read-only comparison in the evaluation container over six active shards (75 KB, 45 rows) reduced schema and row loading from 3.02 to 0.10 seconds; that measurement excludes output writes and manifest publication.

topics.title: [drafting] DSpark drafters for Snowball (Grug-67B-A2B): itw vs targetgen training, serving, and RL status
topics.body:
Related: #9079 (EAGLE-3 PoC), #9114 (adapted EAGLE-3 draft), #9312 (drafting tracker), #9735 (Snowball broad-domain RLVR).

## 1. Overview

We trained two DSpark drafters for [`open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21`](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21) and measured them in vLLM against plain decoding. Both have the same architecture and recipe (3 decoder layers, hidden 2560, FFN 3840, block size 8, 32k draft vocabulary, 280M parameters). They differ in the text they train on, which we call *itw* and *targetgen*:

| | itw drafter | targetgen drafter |
|---|---|---|
| Training text | the gold replies of the Datakit SFT mix (the data the target was fine-tuned on) | the target's own replies (T=1) to 270k sampled Datakit conversations |
| Training length | 80,813 steps, about 9.7B tokens, 21% of one epoch (stopped at a time limit; learning rate not yet decayed) | 17,737 steps, 2.1B tokens, one epoch (learning rate decayed to zero) |
| Compute (2 GB200 nodes) | about 11.7 h of training | 10.2 h of generation + 3.0 h of merge and training |

**Naming.** *itw* (in-the-wild) means the drafter trains on text that already exists, here the replies in the Datakit SFT mix (earlier notes and run names call this "offline" or "off-policy"). *targetgen* (target-generated) means it trains on the target model's own regenerated replies (earlier: "on-policy" or "online").

Main findings:

- Both drafters speed up Snowball decoding: about 1.8x to 2.2x output tokens/s over plain decoding at concurrency 16 (1.5x on later-turn Datakit prompts), with acceptance lengths of 2.8 to 3.1 (2.4 to 2.6 on later turns) (Section 3.1).
- The itw drafter is ahead of the targetgen drafter on every set we measured, by about 0.3 in acceptance length. One epoch of targetgen data did not make up for having 4.6 times fewer training tokens.
- Both drafters transfer to the Dr. Doom fine-tune of the target (acceptance falls by 0.4 to 0.5; the speed-up over plain decoding stays at 1.6x to 1.8x) (Section 3.1).
- The drafter loads in the pinned Marin vLLM fork unchanged. It needs `draft_sample_method: probabilistic` and `rejection_sample_method: standard` set in the serving config for sampled decoding; these are not stored in the checkpoint (Section 4).
- The trainer's validation `accept_len` overstates serving acceptance by about 0.6 to 0.9 tokens, mainly because serving chains its rounds (Section 3.2).
- For RL: the split layout (policy and engines on separate nodes) ran one full RL step with the drafter intact. `colocate_all` does not work with a draft today (acceptance falls to 1.0). The MarinSkyRL change that accepts `dspark` in the managed config is on a [fork branch](https://github.com/atutej/MarinSkyRL/tree/dspark-speculative-decoding) and has not yet been run for several steps (Section 3.4).

## 2. Methodology

### 2.1 Target and drafter

- Target: [`open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21`](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21) (`grug_moe`, hidden 2560, 26 layers, 256 experts), served by vLLM's [`grugmoe.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/39e62869693c46402b1a95fde4fc55ca1aab9ae1/vllm/model_executor/models/grugmoe.py).
- Drafter: DSpark (DFlash plus a Markov logit-bias head and a confidence head), added to vLLM in [vllm-project/vllm#46995](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46995); the draft model class is [`qwen3_dspark.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/39e62869693c46402b1a95fde4fc55ca1aab9ae1/vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_dspark.py). The architecture is set by [`draft_config.json`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/experiments/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_itw/draft_config.json) and the training recipe by [`settings.sh`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/experiments/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_itw/settings.sh):
  - 3 `qwen3`-type layers, FFN 3840 (1.5 x hidden), 20 heads / 5 KV heads, block size 8;
  - hidden states tapped from target layers 2, 12, 22 plus the final layer;
  - 32,000-token draft vocabulary built from the supervised-token frequencies of the training text; the drafter's `lm_head` equals the target's `lm_head` rows for those tokens, bit for bit (checked on both drafters);
  - Markov head rank 256 (vanilla), confidence head; loss 0.1 CE + 0.9 TV against the target's distribution; learning rate 3e-4; 12,288 anchors per 32,768-token sequence.
- Training code: our fork of vllm-project/speculators, branch [`grug-dspark-gate`](https://github.com/atutej/speculators/tree/grug-dspark-gate), with three changes on top of upstream: Grug's gated final norm in the DFlash/DSpark targets and `grug_moe` registration ([f93d1a5](https://github.com/atutej/speculators/commit/f93d1a57998f552a716322925c19eae8d9202342)), `launch_vllm.py` reading the layer count from `config.json` ([96699f9](https://github.com/atutej/speculators/commit/96699f9ad8740040ed18cf2a9443ec33dd740dad)), and HF-style step checkpoints ([99a50bf](https://github.com/atutej/speculators/commit/99a50bf3977776a4a0f5548e5a25e28e6cdd396a)). Not upstream.

### 2.2 Data: the Datakit SFT mix

The training prompts are the data the target was fine-tuned on: the 203-source Datakit SFT mixture. It was downloaded and processed with [`build_datakit_sft_mix.py`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/experiments/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_itw/data/build_datakit_sft_mix.py) (`fetch`, `stats`, `select`, `write`) through [`fetch.sbatch`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/experiments/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_itw/data/fetch.sbatch) / [`submit_fetch.sh`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/experiments/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_itw/data/submit_fetch.sh) and [`write.sbatch`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/experiments/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_itw/data/write.sbatch), following the per-source token allocations in Marin's [`special_token_1000_mix.json`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/82620ad62bbe23b9b12a89d656c24e6f80aff91a/experiments/grug_sft/special_token_1000_mix.json) (commit `82620ad`; the same allocations are on the model repo as [`training_data_mix.json`](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21/blob/main/training_data_mix.json)).

1. Plan. [`plan_datakit_sft_mix.py`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/experiments/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_itw/data/plan_datakit_sft_mix.py) resolves each source to a Hugging Face repo and pinned revision (output [`plan.json`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/experiments/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_itw/data/plan.json); about 628 GB across 160 unique downloads; locations of the normalized outputs in [`normalized_paths.json`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/experiments/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_itw/data/normalized_paths.json)).
2. Fetch and select. Marin's per-source download and normalize steps run through `build_datakit_sft_mix.py fetch`, then `stats` and `select` allocate tokens per source.
3. Write. Render with the Grug chat template, tokenize, clip rows at 32,768 tokens, and write an Arrow dataset of `input_ids` and an assistant-token `loss_mask`; [`finalize_dataset.py`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/experiments/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_itw/data/finalize_dataset.py) checks it and writes the token-frequency file.

Result: 6,471,159 rows in 215 shards, 45.99B tokens after the clip (53.4B before; 313,449 rows were clipped), of which 24.33B tokens are supervised assistant tokens; per-source counts are in the dataset's `manifest.json` ([`training_data_manifest.json`](https://huggingface.co/atutej/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_itw-20261016/blob/main/training_data_manifest.json), also in the targetgen repo). The last 0.1% of rows is held out for validation. The dataset itself is not published; it is rebuilt by the scripts above. Decisions and the Marin commit choice are in [`PLAN.md`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/experiments/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_itw/PLAN.md).

### 2.3 Training setup (both experiments)

Hidden states are extracted online, as in the [Qwen3-0.6B runs](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/experiments/dspark_qwen3_0_6b_nemotron-terminal-corpus_itw/NOTES.md): a vLLM server runs the target and hands hidden states to the trainer through [Mooncake](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake), so nothing is stored on disk. On each of 2 Vista GB200 nodes, 2 GPUs serve the target (TP=1, DP2 x EP2) next to their own `mooncake_master`, and 2 GPUs train; the 4 trainer ranks run as one DDP job. A step is about 120,000 tokens and takes 0.52 s. The entry points are [`vista/run_2node_ddp.sh`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/experiments/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_itw/vista/run_2node_ddp.sh), [`vista/run_2node_ddp.sbatch`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/experiments/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_itw/vista/run_2node_ddp.sbatch) and [`vista/submit_chain.sh`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/experiments/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_itw/vista/submit_chain.sh) (a chain of resumable 12 h jobs). Metrics go to W&B project [`atutej/marin_speculator`](https://wandb.ai/atutej/marin_speculator).

### 2.4 Experiment A: itw drafter

Train on the dataset as written: the gold Datakit replies stand in for the target's completions. One epoch would be 382,747 steps (45.95B tokens); the run was stopped by the time limit at step 80,813 (about 9.7B tokens), so the learning rate (linear decay over the full epoch) had not annealed. The checkpoint we evaluate is `checkpoint-80813`. W&B runs for the three resumed segments: [jgsst5k0](https://wandb.ai/atutej/marin_speculator/runs/jgsst5k0), [71rm9vy8](https://wandb.ai/atutej/marin_speculator/runs/71rm9vy8), [ij7oistz](https://wandb.ai/atutej/marin_speculator/runs/ij7oistz). The trainer's validation `accept_len` at step 80,813 (3.785) is recorded in [`NOTES.md`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/experiments/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_itw/NOTES.md).

### 2.5 Experiment B: targetgen drafter

Same dataset, drafter and recipe, but the supervised text is the target's own. The experiment folder is [`dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_targetgen`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/tree/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/experiments/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_targetgen). It is a chain of two 2-node jobs submitted by `vista/submit_chain.sh`:

1. **Regenerate** (`vista/run_regen.sh` with [`regenerate_token_rows.py`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/tools/regenerate_token_rows.py)). 270,000 rows (4.2% of the train split) are sampled uniformly without replacement. Each node runs its own vLLM (DP4 x EP4, 512 concurrent sequences) on half the rows. For each assistant turn in order, the prompt is everything before it (the original non-assistant tokens plus the target's own earlier turns), the target generates the turn at T=1, top_p=1, up to 32,768 new tokens, stopping at `<|eot_id|>`; the generated tokens (mask 1) replace the original turn, and the original tokens that follow it (tool output, next user turn) are kept with mask 0. A row is cut at 32,768 tokens in total.
2. **Merge and train.** The parts are merged into an Arrow dataset (shuffled), the 32k draft vocabulary is rebuilt from the target's own regenerated tokens (it covers 98.06% of them), and the same 2-node training runs one epoch. The itw run's `run_2node_ddp.sh` is reused with this experiment's settings. The merged dataset has 2.13B tokens. W&B run: [6wnqmuwi](https://wandb.ai/atutej/marin_speculator/runs/6wnqmuwi). The final validation metrics (`accept_len` 3.724) are in [`targetgen_trainer_val_metrics.json`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/docs/results/dspark_eval/targetgen_trainer_val_metrics.json).

Regeneration statistics, from the final lines of the two regeneration logs ([`targetgen_jobs_and_regeneration.txt`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/docs/results/dspark_eval/targetgen_jobs_and_regeneration.txt)): 1.229B generated tokens (about 4,550 per row), 0 errors, 5.0% of rows ended on the 32k per-turn cap, 0.4% ran into the window limit; generation ran at 16.7k to 19.2k tokens/s per node, averaged over the run. In a 3,000-row pilot, 26% of rows were multi-turn (7.4 regenerated turns on average).

We used our own token-level regenerator, not the speculators `regenerate-responses` CLI, because the dataset stores token ids with a loss mask and no chat messages. Going through the CLI means decoding each row back to messages and tools ([`rows_to_messages.py`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/tools/rows_to_messages.py); the round trip is exact on 98.4% of 500 sampled rows) and then training on one row per generation with the whole prefix repeated: 3.8 times more training tokens on a 3,000-row sample, 10.6 times for multi-turn rows ([`boundary_layout_inflation.py`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/tools/boundary_layout_inflation.py); output and the round-trip check in [`regenerate_responses_cli_cost.txt`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/docs/results/dspark_eval/regenerate_responses_cli_cost.txt)).

### 2.6 Evaluation

Every arm serves the target in the pinned Marin vLLM fork, [`marin-vllm-gpu-20260929-39e62869693c`](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/releases/tag/marin-vllm-gpu-20260929-39e62869693c), the same wheel [MarinSkyRL pins](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/blob/8ab8f3a7b44c9828efd8c41a88d5fa2f8eab9a68/pyproject.toml#L100). Settings are `--tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel` on one GB200 node, one server at a time on an otherwise idle node, concurrency 16, T=1, top_p=1. The drafter arms use `{"method": "dspark", "num_speculative_tokens": 8, "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic", "rejection_sample_method": "standard"}`; plain decoding is the baseline. Concurrency 16 matches the `max_num_seqs: 16` per engine in the RL config ([`glm53_rlvr1_antidoom_reference_kl.yaml`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-broad-domain-rlvr-campaign-2026/blob/main/configs/glm53_rlvr1_antidoom_reference_kl.yaml)).

- Acceptance length is `1 + accepted/drafts` from vLLM's speculative-decoding counters, using the definition in speculators' [`perf_utils.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/speculators/blob/main/scripts/evaluate/perf_utils.py), over the whole chained rollout.
- Throughput is generated tokens divided by wall time for the whole set; the gain is the ratio to the plain-decoding arm on the same prompts.
- Harness: [`serve_eval.sh`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/tools/eval_acceptance/serve_eval.sh) (one server per arm) and [`run_eval.py`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/tools/eval_acceptance/run_eval.py) (prompts, sampling, counters); for batch jobs, [`eval_arms.sbatch`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/tools/eval_acceptance/eval_arms.sbatch) and [`submit_eval.sh`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/tools/eval_acceptance/submit_eval.sh).

Prompt sets (manifests with seeds and hashes: [`docs/results/dspark_eval/prompt_manifests/`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/tree/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/docs/results/dspark_eval/prompt_manifests)):

- **(a) RL prompts.** Rows of the Snowball broad-domain RLVR training set, [`open-athena/Nemotron-RL-Ultra-RLVR1-Cleaned-v3-2026-09-30`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Nemotron-RL-Ultra-RLVR1-Cleaned-v3-2026-09-30) (the corrected preparation described in the campaign's [`CLEANED_DATASET.md`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-broad-domain-rlvr-campaign-2026/blob/main/audits/CLEANED_DATASET.md); train split), rendered as the RL requests carry them: stored messages (including earlier assistant tool calls and tool outputs), each row's tool schemas (the `request_json` column) passed as `tools=`, and the chat template's default `Reasoning: /think` (the [RL config](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-broad-domain-rlvr-campaign-2026/blob/main/configs/glm53_rlvr1_antidoom_reference_kl.yaml) passes no `chat_template_kwargs`; the [template](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21/blob/main/chat_template.jinja) defaults to `/think`). Generation settings follow the same config: up to 49,152 new tokens per turn, 102,400-token window, T=1. 1,024 prompts sampled at random; we ran the first 256, which are themselves a uniform sample. Mix of the 1,024: tool use 389, instruction following 148, code 94, math 55, MCQA 44, MultiChallenge 41, others; 229 prompts already contain tool-call history. Built by [`build_nemotron_rlvr_prompts.py`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/tools/eval_acceptance/build_nemotron_rlvr_prompts.py).
- **(b) Datakit validation prompts, multi-turn.** 1,024 prompts from the 6,472 held-out Datakit rows, which neither drafter trained on. For each row a uniformly random assistant turn is chosen, with the dataset's earlier turns as context: 833 first-turn and 191 later-turn prompts (median context 3,119 tokens, longest 27,450). Replies capped at 4,096 tokens. Built by [`build_val_prompts.py --turns random`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/tools/eval_acceptance/build_val_prompts.py).
- **(c) Dr. Doom target.** The same RL-prompt run with the target replaced by [`open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21-dr-doom`](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21-dr-doom) (the FTPO de-looping fine-tune). Both drafters were trained against the 09.21 hidden states, so this measures transfer to a fine-tuned target.

### 2.7 RL integration

MarinSkyRL (pin [`5de48d34`](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/commit/5de48d34), vLLM wheel as above) was run on Vista GB200 with the DSpark drafter in an R2E-Gym RL setup. The infrastructure notes are in [`docs/rl_dspark_infra.md`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/docs/rl_dspark_infra.md) and the A/B notes in [`r2egym-rl-ab/NOTES.md`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/rl_speculation/experiments/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_r2egym-rl-ab/NOTES.md). The two layouts are [`2node_grug_datakit_dspark_r2egym_rl.yaml`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/rl_speculation/configs/2node_grug_datakit_dspark_r2egym_rl.yaml) (split, `weight_sync_transport: expert_block`) and [`…_rl_coloc.yaml`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/rl_speculation/configs/2node_grug_datakit_dspark_r2egym_rl_coloc.yaml) (`colocate_all`). The managed [`generator.speculative_decoding`](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/blob/8ab8f3a7b44c9828efd8c41a88d5fa2f8eab9a68/marinskyrl/speculative_decoding.py#L26-L29) block accepts only `eagle3`. A branch on a fork, [`atutej/MarinSkyRL:dspark-speculative-decoding`](https://github.com/atutej/MarinSkyRL/tree/dspark-speculative-decoding), adds three commits on top of Marin main: `dspark` as a method ([203c6f9d](https://github.com/atutej/MarinSkyRL/commit/203c6f9d909307e8f6ac288f9d320f349c43bb8b)), optional `draft_sample_method` / `rejection_sample_method` fields ([d2c23a89](https://github.com/atutej/MarinSkyRL/commit/d2c23a8921658aaf8a8d9211dbcc693d9a9490c8)), and the post-weight-sync refresh of the draft head for `dspark` ([9a0ea386](https://github.com/atutej/MarinSkyRL/commit/9a0ea386eaf6ccc35391ebe3fba2d5744a3f2cb6)).

## 3. Results

### 3.1 Acceptance length and throughput

**(a) RL prompts**, 09.21 target, first 256 prompts, replies up to 49,152 tokens (mean about 11k tokens, 11.7% hit the cap). Raw results: [`docs/results/dspark_eval/rl_prompts_256_target-09.21/`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/tree/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/docs/results/dspark_eval/rl_prompts_256_target-09.21).

| Arm | Acceptance length | Output tokens/s | Gain vs plain |
|---|---|---|---|
| Plain decoding | n/a | 1,960 | 1.00x |
| itw drafter, step 80,813 | **3.141** | 4,226 | **2.16x** |
| targetgen drafter, step 17,737 | 2.835 | 3,696 | 1.89x |

**(a2) RL prompts on the Dr. Doom target** ([`open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21-dr-doom`](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21-dr-doom)), same 256 prompts and settings (replies up to 49,152 tokens; mean about 16k tokens, 20.7% hit the cap). Raw results: [`docs/results/dspark_eval/rl_prompts_256_target-dr-doom/`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/tree/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/docs/results/dspark_eval/rl_prompts_256_target-dr-doom).

| Arm | Acceptance length | Output tokens/s | Gain vs plain |
|---|---|---|---|
| Plain decoding | n/a | 2,023 | 1.00x |
| itw drafter, step 80,813 | **2.667** | 3,630 | **1.79x** |
| targetgen drafter, step 17,737 | 2.465 | 3,270 | 1.62x |

Both drafters were trained on the 09.21 target's hidden states, so this is transfer to a fine-tuned target. Acceptance falls by 0.47 (itw) and 0.37 (targetgen) relative to table (a), and the speed-up over plain decoding stays at 1.6x to 1.8x. The ordering of the two drafters is the same.

**(b) Datakit validation prompts, multi-turn**, 09.21 target, 1,024 prompts, replies up to 4,096 tokens. Raw results: [`docs/results/dspark_eval/datakit_val_multiturn_1024/`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/tree/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/docs/results/dspark_eval/datakit_val_multiturn_1024).

| Subset | Plain tok/s | itw: acceptance length | tok/s | gain | targetgen: acceptance length | tok/s | gain |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| First turn (833) | 2,131 | **3.188** | 4,401 | **2.07x** | 2.879 | 4,004 | 1.88x |
| Later turn (191) | 1,613 | **2.601** | 2,529 | **1.57x** | 2.373 | 2,339 | 1.45x |
| Pooled (1,024) | 2,066 | **3.122** | 4,113 | **1.99x** | 2.821 | 3,749 | 1.81x |

Supplementary, earlier runs with the same harness (raw results: [`docs/results/dspark_eval/r2egym_1024_greedy/`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/tree/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/docs/results/dspark_eval/r2egym_1024_greedy)): on 1,024 R2E-Gym first-turn prompts with greedy drafting the two drafters are close (acceptance length 2.245 for the itw and 2.321 for the targetgen drafter; gains 1.51x and 1.54x). Later turns are harder than first turns for both drafters (Table b).

### 3.2 Trainer metric versus serving

The validation `accept_len` the trainer logs is 3.785 (itw, step 80,813, on Datakit validation rows; [`NOTES.md`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/experiments/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_itw/NOTES.md)) and 3.724 (targetgen, final, on its own held-out rows; [`targetgen_trainer_val_metrics.json`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/docs/results/dspark_eval/targetgen_trainer_val_metrics.json)). Serving gives less, for two reasons we could separate:

- The trainer averages the accepted length of one draft round started at each of many positions, equally weighted. Serving chains rounds: after a long accepted run it skips an easy stretch, after a short one it stays in the hard spot, so its number is closer to a harmonic mean. Measured with the same text, a single round from uniformly random positions in the target's own replies gives 3.642 (itw) and 3.271 (targetgen) ([raw probe results](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/tree/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/docs/results/dspark_eval/random_anchor_probe_target_replies)), against 3.122 and 2.826 chained on the same Datakit validation prompts with probabilistic drafting ([raw results](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/tree/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/docs/results/dspark_eval/datakit_val_firstturn_1024_probabilistic)). On the targetgen run's own held-out rows (long multi-turn contexts, supervised anchors) the one-round numbers are 3.855 and 3.501 ([raw probe results](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/tree/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/docs/results/dspark_eval/random_anchor_probe_heldout_targetgen_rows)).
- Greedy drafting costs about 0.3 more than probabilistic drafting (for the itw drafter 2.660 against 2.973 on an earlier 128-prompt set; see [`NOTES.md`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/experiments/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_itw/NOTES.md)).

Teacher-forced parity between the trainer's drafter and vLLM's drafter was checked: they pick the same token in 97 to 98% of slots, with equal acceptance on common anchors, so we found no implementation mismatch (also in `NOTES.md`). One residual remains unexplained: on its own held-out rows the targetgen drafter reaches 3.50 in the one-round probe against the trainer's 3.72. The probe is [`probe_random_anchor.py`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/tools/eval_acceptance/probe_random_anchor.py) with the launcher [`probe_serve.sh`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/tools/eval_acceptance/probe_serve.sh).

### 3.3 Cost

| | itw | targetgen |
|---|---|---|
| Generation | none | 10.2 h on 2 nodes (1.23B tokens) |
| Merge and training | about 11.7 h of training for 80,813 steps | 3.0 h for 17,737 steps (includes about 0.5 h merge) |
| Training tokens | about 9.7B | 2.1B |

The targetgen budget was chosen to match the itw run's wall time (about 12 to 14 h on 2 nodes). The two runs are not matched in training tokens or in learning-rate schedule. Job records: Slurm accounting for the targetgen chain (regen 10:14:45, train 03:02:50) in [`targetgen_jobs_and_regeneration.txt`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/docs/results/dspark_eval/targetgen_jobs_and_regeneration.txt).

### 3.4 RL status

- **Split layout** (policy on one node, one DP4 x EP4 engine on another, [`weight_sync_transport: expert_block`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/rl_speculation/configs/2node_grug_datakit_dspark_r2egym_rl.yaml), Triton MoE backend): one RL step ran end to end with the drafter intact (accept length 2.54 in the step-1 rollouts; the weight sync after training took 1.5 s). The default broadcast sync ran out of memory in this layout. The run failed later in a way we have not diagnosed, so we do not yet have acceptance after a weight sync. Details: [`docs/rl_dspark_infra.md`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/docs/rl_dspark_infra.md).
- **`colocate_all`** ([config](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/rl_speculation/configs/2node_grug_datakit_dspark_r2egym_rl_coloc.yaml)): the draft did not survive. Accept length was 1.000 in both runs. Engines sleep during training, and a [probe](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/rl_speculation/tools/sleep_wake_probe.py) showed that sleep level 2 discards the draft's weights; our level-1 [patch](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/setup/machines/vista/patches/marinskyrl-sleep-level.patch) is not confirmed in an RL run. The managed `speculative_decoding` block rejects `colocate_all=true` at launch; our colocated runs passed `speculative_config` through the engine kwargs directly, which bypasses that check.
- **Draft head after weight sync:** MarinSkyRL re-slices the draft's `lm_head` from the updated policy after each sync, but only for [`eagle3`](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/blob/8ab8f3a7b44c9828efd8c41a88d5fa2f8eab9a68/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/inference_engines/vllm/vllm_engine.py#L594), using vLLM's [`refresh_target_owned_draft_weights`](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/39e62869693c46402b1a95fde4fc55ca1aab9ae1/vllm/v1/spec_decode/online_eagle.py#L89). The DSpark drafter's head is the same kind of frozen slice (bit-identical to the target's rows), so [the fork branch](https://github.com/atutej/MarinSkyRL/commit/9a0ea386eaf6ccc35391ebe3fba2d5744a3f2cb6) extends the refresh to `dspark`. The refresh has not been exercised in a multi-step RL run.
- The drafter is not trained during RL, so acceptance is expected to decay as the policy moves away from the 09.21 weights.

### 3.5 Limitations

- We have not run RL with these drafters yet; Section 3.4 is the state of that work.
- In MarinSkyRL, colocating the draft with the policy (`colocate_all`) currently disables it: acceptance falls to 1.0.

## 4. Artifacts and reproduction

- Drafters (`config.json`, `config.py`, `model.safetensors` each), uploaded with [`upload_drafter_to_hf.py`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments/blob/91e20d39f5f4bc62f956d6a9e0e67b7dcbb1ab74/pipelines/speculator_training/tools/upload_drafter_to_hf.py): [`atutej/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_itw-20261016`](https://huggingface.co/atutej/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_itw-20261016) and [`atutej/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_targetgen-20261016`](https://huggingface.co/atutej/dspark_grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft_datakit-sft-mix_targetgen-20261016)
- Serving recipe, tested with the pinned fork [`marin-vllm-gpu-20260929-39e62869693c`](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/releases/tag/marin-vllm-gpu-20260929-39e62869693c):

  ```
  vllm serve open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
    --speculative-config '{"method": "dspark", "model": "<drafter repo>", "num_speculative_tokens": 8,
                           "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic", "rejection_sample_method": "standard"}'
  ```
  The fork needs no changes: vLLM reads the checkpoint's `speculators_config` with its own [parser](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/39e62869693c46402b1a95fde4fc55ca1aab9ae1/vllm/transformers_utils/configs/speculators/base.py) and does not import the `speculators` package. The sampling fields are not stored in the checkpoint.
- Code: [`atutej/spec-experiments`](https://github.com/atutej/spec-experiments) (branch `grug-full-run-and-rl`, commit `91e20d3`), [`atutej/speculators@grug-dspark-gate`](https://github.com/atutej/speculators/tree/grug-dspark-gate), [`atutej/MarinSkyRL@dspark-speculative-decoding`](https://github.com/atutej/MarinSkyRL/tree/dspark-speculative-decoding).
- W&B: project [`atutej/marin_speculator`](https://wandb.ai/atutej/marin_speculator).

topics.title: Evaluate a copy-paste output head on July MoE at d512 and d768
topics.body:
Evaluate Copy-Paste Language Models on the original July MoE recipe. The copy head mixes the native vocabulary distribution with a causal distribution over observed tokens, sums repeated-token mass, and uses a learned sink to fall back to the vocabulary head. Packed documents remain isolated. Method: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19247v1.

The first d512, seed-0 validation at 1,000 updates improved the 23-domain macro NLL from 4.579368 to 4.092498 (-0.486869, 10.63%); all 23 domains improved. Native aggregate NLL was 4.387551 versus 3.858693. This is an early, single-seed observation, not a final quality or efficiency claim. The 10,980-update run is still running.

The paired protocol preserves the original July backbone, initialization, QB routing, MuonH/AdamH/Adam optimizer, sequence8192, batch16, tokenizer, training mixture and native validation. Recipe commit: 444b5ea66bda75b6dfc7746ff20c9dfec6ba159a; runtime: 3fd402a926c907d7cb87a04935e56db972652c48. The tiled target-only head adds 525,312 parameters at d512 and avoids materializing a batch × sequence × vocabulary copy distribution. Its attention arithmetic remains quadratic; speedup is not claimed.

Extend the comparison to d768, reusing completed control 2c7b6faaf611ba8ca4c0. This control has six layers, six query heads, one KV head, expert384/shared768 and deliberately retains the d512 optimizer heuristic. The candidate must keep that recipe, with 1,181,184 added copy-head parameters. Both widths use 10,980 updates (1,439,170,560 input tokens), seed0 and reserved v4-32. Report final and intermediate NLL, all domains, raw loss curves, wall time and throughput; do not equate token matching with compute matching.

Independent dense-mixture checks cover values, all six gradient paths, repeated/absent targets, future/document isolation and disabled-gate parity. All four d512 TPU workers passed BF16 fused-head checks before training. The synthetic precursor reduced loss but failed complete-output evaluation; it did not pass a task mastery gate.

Implementation/evidence: https://github.com/WhenWen/astra-d8-research/pull/152
Frozen protocol: https://github.com/WhenWen/astra-d8-research/blob/codex/cplm-july-moe/research/cplm-july-moe-protocol.md
First curves and raw-evidence pointers: https://github.com/WhenWen/astra-d8-research/blob/codex/cplm-july-moe/research/cplm-july-results.md
Live d512 run: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/auto-understanding-arch/runs/seed0-v1

The upstream contribution will keep the opt-in copy head and numerical tests separate from the default recipe. Generation/cache support and multiple-seed replication remain outside this initial NLL experiment. A merged implementation does not settle the research question.

Research provenance: https://github.com/WhenWen/astra-d8-research/issues/151; originating task definition: https://github.com/WhenWen/astra-d8-research/issues/99 (`ordered_paragraph_template@1`). Prior synthetic findings: https://github.com/WhenWen/astra-d8-research/issues/149. These task records provide provenance; the July experiment evaluates native LM data.

comments.body:
🤖
# Research

Low-effort prior work: the [CPLM paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19247v1) reports gains on other backbones, while this issue reports a 10.63% d512 macro-NLL reduction at 1,000 updates across 23 domains; the full d512 result and paired d768 candidate are still unreported here. Marin's current model uses a fused native-vocabulary loss, and searches for `10229` and `CPLM` found no open Marin implementation PR. The linked research PR, frozen protocol, and W&B run were inaccessible to this session, so their current state and exact measurements remain unverified.

**Relevant code**
- [`model.py#L731-L747`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5e12684c85eac9295514a4c8cdbfee0a55ad497c/experiments/grug/moe/model.py#L731-L747) — native loss path
- [`train.py#L173-L193`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5e12684c85eac9295514a4c8cdbfee0a55ad497c/experiments/grug/moe/train.py#L173-L193) — tagged per-domain evaluation
- [`launch.py#L207-L246`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5e12684c85eac9295514a4c8cdbfee0a55ad497c/experiments/grug/moe/launch.py#L207-L246) — current upstream recipe wiring

# Proposed Fix

1. Recover the linked protocol and pin the exact recipe/runtime commits, dataset and tokenizer identities, validation domains, seeds, optimizer settings, and control/candidate checkpoint IDs for both widths; confirm the d768 control is `2c7b6faaf611ba8ca4c0` and preserve its d512 optimizer heuristic.
2. Before a d768 run, verify the tiled target-only head against a dense reference for values, six gradient paths, repeated and absent targets, future and packed-document isolation, and disabled-gate parity; repeat the BF16 fused-head check on the target v4-32 setup.
3. Finish or recover the d512 candidate through 10,980 updates, then run the d768 candidate for the same 10,980 updates, seed 0, sequence 8192, and batch 16 on reserved v4-32, changing only the opt-in copy head against each width's control.
4. Publish intermediate and final paired NLL for all 23 domains and both aggregates, raw loss curves, exact token counts, wall time, throughput, parameter and copy-attention cost, and links to immutable configs/checkpoints; distinguish token-matched from compute-matched comparisons.
5. Decide from the final paired results whether the NLL gain justifies measured overhead, then submit a separate opt-in Marin implementation with numerical tests if warranted; leave generation/cache support and replication as explicit follow-ups.

🤖 Draft implementation: #10230. The d768 candidate `428ab40bd4f65ab8758b` is allocated a separate reserved v4-32 slice and its four workers are building; no d768 loss is available yet. It reuses completed d768 control `2c7b6faaf611ba8ca4c0` without retraining. d512 continues: at 2,000 updates, 23-domain macro NLL is 3.901824 versus 4.278339 (-0.376514); 2,600 training observations are retained with no gaps or non-finite losses. Updated raw curves: https://github.com/WhenWen/astra-d8-research/blob/codex/cplm-july-moe/research/cplm-july/update2000/loss-curves.png . These remain intermediate seed-0 comparisons.

🤖 Numerical audit clarification: the pinned research runtime also defaults vocabulary CE to streaming XLA. The research adapter reconstructs log Z using CE plus an FP32 target dot, while XLA obtains the target through matrix multiplication. These are algebraically equivalent but not guaranteed bit-exact. Both runs passed their frozen BF16 value/gradient preflights on all four workers (maximum tested NLL error 0.0009327), which is finite-shape evidence, not an exactness guarantee for all trained states. The upstream PR now exposes only the backend-independent loss and requires caller-supplied NLL/log partition; the frozen training implementations are unchanged. This caveat is recorded in the dated protocol amendment.

🤖 D768 training launch confirmed: run 428ab40bd4f65ab8758b completed four optimizer updates in the retained startup snapshot, with finite losses and all four TPU workers running on a separate v4-32 slice. All four small-shape BF16 preflight checks passed. Full schedule: 10,980 updates; no wall-clock cap. Live run: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/auto-understanding-arch/runs/cplm-july-d768-seed0-v1 . Initial curves and evidence: https://github.com/WhenWen/astra-d8-research/tree/codex/cplm-july-moe/research/cplm-july-d768 . Validation starts at update1,000; no d768 quality conclusion yet. Upstream draft #10230 has green CI; five direct numerical tests also pass.

🤖 Final seed-0 results, 2026-10-17 Pacific

Both original-July CPLM runs completed 10,980 optimizer updates / 1,439,170,560 input tokens on TPU v4-32. Historical controls were reused; no baseline was retrained.

topics.title: Add a tiled copy-paste loss for July MoE experiments
topics.body:
Add a target-only copy-paste loss for July MoE experiments. To predict token t+1, the head attends only to observed tokens at positions ≤t in the same packed document and sums repeated-token probability. The copy gate competes with the vocabulary logits; a learned sink returns part of the copy probability to the native vocabulary distribution. Rematerialized query tiles bound score storage while retaining quadratic arithmetic.

The loss accepts native vocabulary NLL and log partition with gradients, leaving vocabulary-kernel choice and loss masking to the caller. Independent dense-mixture tests cover values, gradients and causal/document isolation. The historical July training adapter and d512/d768 run evidence are linked from the issue. This initial draft does not integrate with the current trainer or provide optimized vocabulary kernels or generation/cache support. Current Marin's vocabulary backend selection differs from the pinned research runtime and needs separate integration checks.

Part of #10229.

Research provenance: https://github.com/WhenWen/astra-d8-research/issues/151 and originating task https://github.com/WhenWen/astra-d8-research/issues/99 (`ordered_paragraph_template@1`).

topics.title: [post-training] Explore computer-use agents with text and code interfaces
topics.body:
TL;DR

Marin has not trained or evaluated any model on computer use: operating desktop, mobile or browser applications. Two Alibaba papers from this week release pieces a text-only model could use. This issue proposes RL on MAI-Gym's 42 synthetic apps through their text observation mode, and a computer-use baseline on OSWorld-v2 with OpenGCUA's code-first harness. Pixel-based tasks wait for vision support. No experiments have run yet.

Marin's agent post-training covers function calling, terminal and SWE tasks. Nothing covers graphical applications:

- No computer-use benchmark (OSWorld, AndroidWorld, WebArena) appears in the current eval policy ([#10197](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10197)). The nearest evals are the terminal benchmarks Terminal-Bench 2.1 and OT-TBLite.
- The harnesses we train and evaluate with (Terminus-2, Pi, mini-swe-agent, OpenCode) expose shell, file and function-call tools only. On these tasks, the Antidoom step-12 checkpoint of Snowball, Marin's post-trained 67B-A2B MoE, scores 31.1% on SWE-bench Verified and 10.9% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 ([#10040](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10040#issuecomment-6158094013)).
- [#7418](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7418) listed the web and OS agent sources from OpenThoughts-Agent (Mind2Web, go-browse, Synatra, nnetnav-live, AgentTuning WebShop/ALFWorld/OS). It left them unconverted because they need an interactive runtime to verify. All are text-only. The issue closed on October 6 in favour of sourcing our own RL data.
- Our models cannot read screenshots. Rui Li's SigLIP2 + Qwen3 baseline ([#2383](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/2383)) did not merge. bkolligs is connecting SigLIP to Delphi 998M ([#9524](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9524), [PR #10076](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10076), open) and has no benchmark numbers yet.
- Shellbox machines return text and bytes only ([`machine.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5e12684c85eac9295514a4c8cdbfee0a55ad497c/lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/machine.py#L211-L248)). The QEMU backend is a headless microVM, and nobody has measured whether `/dev/kvm` is available on our nodes ([#9433](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9433)).
- Our largest sandbox run reached about 2,150 live gVisor sandboxes before the controller of Iris, our cluster scheduler, saturated ([#10111](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10111)). Work to move execution off the controller is open ([#10119](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10119)).

TaskForge ([#10152](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10152)), our RL task generator, validates each task by replaying reference solutions and running agents that look for shortcuts. Its tasks so far are math and science problems in shells.

MAI-Gym

[MAI-Gym](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20939) (Tong et al., 2026) runs GUI agents for evaluation and online RL through one rollout pipeline:

- Environments: Android in ReDroid containers, which avoids the nested virtualization the standard emulator needs; desktop VMs inside containers; headless Chromium for web. It reaches 20,000 parallel instances with warm pools and screenshots passed through object storage.
- Actions: coordinate clicks, typing and hotkeys, plus `bash` on desktops. Observations are screenshots, plus shell output on desktops.
- Synthetic apps: coding agents build resettable mock apps and cross-app scenarios. A verifier must score 0 on the initial state, 1 after a reference solution and 0 after reset.
- Training: Qwen3.5-9B (a vision-language model), SFT then GRPO. MAI-Gym-9B scores 76.2% on OSWorld-Verified (desktop) and 78.4% on MobileWorld (Android).
- Transfer: RL in a mock of the 12306 train-ticketing app raised success on 52 tasks in the real app, on a physical phone, from 28.8% to 48.1%.

Only part of it is released. The repository has the agent harness and 42 synthetic apps with 840 tasks. The framework, the synthesis skills and the 2,000 OSWorld/MobileWorld tasks are announced but not yet published.

Each released app is one HTML file with a deterministic state machine. Its manifest declares a text observation (`engine.a11y(state)`) and actions by element ID (`tap {id}`, `type {id, text}`). Verifiers are JSON checks on the app's final state. A text-only model can therefore run these tasks in a headless browser, with no screenshots.

OpenGCUA

[OpenGCUA](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22200) (Zhou et al., 2026) studies harness design for computer use with existing frontier models. It releases no trained model.

- At each step the model writes one Python program. The program may call `pyautogui`, `bash()` and `subprocess`, and the prompt prefers `bash()` to GUI actions.
- The paper moves two decisions from fixed harness rules to the model: when to take a screenshot, and how to track task state, which the model does with a todo list.
- On the 82 OSWorld-v2 tasks that need no internet access, the mean partial score of eight models rose from 45.3 with GUI-only batched actions to 64.9 with this code-first harness. Steps per task fell 53%. The weakest GUI-only models gained the most: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash rose from 28.0 to 57.7.

The paper runs no text-only configuration, so we analysed its released trajectories. Models requested a screenshot in 26–60% of steps. Each model used no GUI actions on 4 to 18 tasks, and only 5 of the 82 tasks were solved by some model with neither GUI actions nor screenshots. A text-only model would solve few of these tasks, but the shell-first design matches what our models already do well.

Licences

- MAI-Gym's repository has no licence file, so the apps and tasks need the authors' permission before we train on them.
- OpenGCUA's code is Apache-2.0. Its trajectories carry no licence, and most are outputs of closed models.
- OSWorld-v2 is Apache-2.0.

Goal: give Marin a computer-use evaluation and a first training signal for graphical applications, starting with interfaces a text-only model can use.

Hypotheses:

1. RL on a training split of MAI-Gym's synthetic apps, using text observations, raises Snowball's success on held-out apps. Function calling (BFCL-Parity), Terminal-Bench 2.1 and SWE-bench Verified do not regress.
2. With OpenGCUA's code-first harness and no screenshots, Snowball solves some of the 82 offline OSWorld-v2 tasks. That score is the text-only baseline a vision-capable model must beat.

Proposed steps:

1. Ask the MAI-Gym authors about licensing the apps and tasks.
2. Run the 42 apps in a headless browser behind a Shellbox backend that exposes the text observation and ID actions, with the existing verifiers as rewards. Hold out whole apps for evaluation, and check the tasks with TaskForge's validation. The same backend could later host the web sources from #7418.
3. Measure the Snowball baseline on the held-out apps, then run RL with Marin's rollout engine ([#9623](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9623)).
4. Check whether `/dev/kvm` is available on our Iris nodes. If it is, run OSWorld-v2 with the OpenGCUA harness in a desktop VM. Without KVM, the QEMU backend falls back to software emulation (TCG), which is slower.
5. Revisit pixel-based tasks when [#9524](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9524) produces a vision model at a useful scale.

Proposed. No owner yet. Computer use is not on any current roadmap.

Links

* Papers: [MAI-Gym, arXiv 2610.20939](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20939); [OpenGCUA, arXiv 2610.22200](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22200)
* MAI-Gym code and apps: [Tongyi-MAI/MAI-Gym](https://github.com/Tongyi-MAI/MAI-Gym) (apps in `site/apps/`); model: [Tongyi-MAI/MAI-Gym-9B](https://huggingface.co/Tongyi-MAI/MAI-Gym-9B)
* OpenGCUA code: [Tongyi-MAI/OpenGCUA](https://github.com/Tongyi-MAI/OpenGCUA) (OSWorld agents in `packages/harness/examples/osworld/`); trajectories: [viewer](https://tongyi-mai.github.io/OpenGCUA/trajectories.html)
* Benchmark: [xlang-ai/OSWorld-V2](https://github.com/xlang-ai/OSWorld-V2)
* Android containers: [ReDroid](https://github.com/remote-android/redroid-doc)
* Related: [#10189](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10189) (web-search agents)

---

topics.title: [levanter] LM evaluation fails with explicitly context-sharded tokens
topics.body:
Held-out LM evaluation fails when token positions are explicitly sharded across a context mesh. Training updates succeed; the first evaluation raises:

```text
lib/levanter/src/levanter/eval.py:238, _default_lm_eval_loss_fn
per_pos_token_id = jnp.roll(named_batch.tokens.array, -1, axis=-1)
ShardingTypeError: `a` cannot be sharded on the axis being rolled over.
Got arr type=i32[16@(replica_dcn,data,expert),32768@context] and axis=(1,)
```

Reproduce:
1. Use an explicit mesh with local axes `data=1, replica=1, model=1, expert=8` and inter-node axes `replica_dcn=1, context=4` (32 GPUs).
2. Map `batch` to `(replica_dcn,data,expert)` and `position` to `context`, with global batch 16 and sequence length 32,768.
3. Run `cb_tagged_lm_evaluate` on a model and batch with that layout. Its default loss callback reaches the failing roll.

Expected: target-token shifting and token-weighted evaluation agree with an unsharded reference. The training loss path in `models/loss.py` already gathers the token IDs along the sharded position axis before shifting and restores their layout afterward.

Observed in the #10213 sweep at completed update 548, its first held-out evaluation, on base commit `753bbb163c78f0e7ea50059522f42156708162c8` plus experiment-local changes. Iris job: `/karan/task203-lr1e6-20261017-r3/snowball-v0-pilot-sft`. Retrieve the error with `uv run iris --cluster=marin task logs /karan/task203-lr1e6-20261017-r3/snowball-v0-pilot-sft/1 --substring ShardingTypeError`.

The labeled callback contains the same roll at `eval.py:277`; that path was not exercised in this run. This issue tracks the shared evaluator fix separately from moving the sweep's validation offline.

🤖 # Research

Both default LM evaluation callbacks call `jnp.roll` on token arrays whose position axis may be explicitly sharded. JAX rejects that roll before the evaluator can aggregate loss or byte counts. The evaluator already receives the mesh mapping needed to restore the token layout after shifting.

**Relevant code**
- [`eval.py#L223-L237`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/eval.py#L223-L237) — tagged callback token shift
- [`eval.py#L259-L276`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/eval.py#L259-L276) — labeled callback token shift
- [`eval.py#L531-L577`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/eval.py#L531-L577) — token IDs feed byte aggregation

# Proposed Fix

`TaggedEvaluator.accum_for_batch()` or `LabeledEvaluator.accum_for_batch()` → default loss callback → `jnp.roll` on context-sharded positions → `ShardingTypeError`. Replicate the position axis for the shift, then restore its mapped sharding in both default callbacks; verify token IDs and token-weighted metrics against an unsharded reference on a small context mesh.

🤖 Fix is open in #10233. Both default callbacks use the training loss's sharding-safe token shift, and byte lookup keeps an explicit output layout for context shards. Two-device CPU regressions match unsharded tagged loss and bits-per-byte metrics and labeled next-token IDs; the focused evaluator and loss suite passed 23 tests. The full Levanter run hit an unrelated Grug MoE test that uses `ragged-all-to-all`, which XLA:CPU does not support; all-files Pyrefly reported missing optional imports outside the changed files.

topics.title: Marin eval policy roadmap
topics.body:
OVERVIEW

Our first task for you concerns the next iteration of our eval policy! As you are no doubt aware, we are very excited to have you help create and source new high quality evals for Marin, and help direct our eval policy. We have many directions we are excited to explore that the current iteration either does not cover, or covers with insufficient granularity.

Therefore, your first assignment at Marin is to create a *roadmap* for Marin’s eval policy. Look into the details of the current policy and consider -- what, in your estimation, are the most crucial areas for us to improve upon? Here are some candidates we could consider; please treat these as suggestions or starting points, not as mandates. You are free to pick your own priorities. Also, please treat this as an unordered set rather than an ordered priority list!

OPEN QUESTIONS

1. Marin currently does not explicitly evaluate the multilingual capabilities of its models under the policy. This stands in contrast to projects like OpenEuroLLM, which are explicitly emphasizing multilingual ability. There are many evals of this type we could consider including, such as [JudgeArena](https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/JudgeArena). We could also start evaluating our models’ capabilities in the realm of culturally idiomatic language.
2. simpleQA (or a miniaturized version of it) is a benchmark we are excited to evaluate under our policy, because we believe it has the potential to correlate well with our out-of-distribution AAII target. That said, our current implementation of simpleQA is producing extremely depressed estimates of model capability. We believe this warrants some investigation; a repaired simpleQA would be a useful addition to our cohort.
3. We should consider adding a more realistic long context eval to our policy to complement MRCR and give a more holistic picture of our models’ retrieval capability.
4. We currently do not evaluate deep research or search capability directly.
5. We lack a comprehensive overview of the long tail of agentic benchmarks which now appear in many frontier labs’ model cards. Should we consider adding some of these to our policy?
6. IFBench scores are depressed and do not seem likely to be a realistic reflection of model instruction following capabilities; a well-designed benchmark derived from the [Snowball conversation lab](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/snowball-conversation-lab) might be a good replacement for this.
7. We have several biology / medical benchmarks we could consider incorporating into future eval policies; biomedical knowledge: MedXpertQA or PubMedQA, Clinical reasoning: HealthBench Professional/ Bedside Bench /ASCENT, Biological discovery: Longevity — genetics regression; LAB-Bench cloning / DNA methylation age comparison, Medical coding: MedConceptsQA — ATC Hard/ MedConceptsQA ICD-10 procedures, hard

DONE WHEN

We have a document that proposes a priority list of what we should focus on in our next eval policy (limitations) and sketches out potential solutions. Ideally, the document will also include an estimated timeline for the next eval policy release.

REFERENCES:

Marin Eval Policy 10-16-26: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10197

Snowball V0 vs Baselines -> issue 10199

Review the existing eight agent tasks for missing capabilities, and coordinate any new biomedical task with [#9258](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258), where grading ambiguity and coverage are still open.
5. **November 23–30: freeze and release.** Select only pilots that pass the admission sheet, pin data/prompts/judges/serving configs, run the complete baseline cohort, preserve traces, and meet the policy's ≥90% scored-trial coverage rule. Publish per-benchmark scores with uncertainty, costs, failed/graded coverage, ID/OOD status, and the reasons for deferring each candidate. If a full cohort or audit misses the gate, move the release date rather than publish a partial canonical panel.

topics.title: [evals] Use strong-model sampling to discover coverage gaps
topics.body:
<!-- experiment-tldr:start -->
## Summary

This experiment explored whether free generation from strong base models can reveal pretraining coverage gaps that ordinary evals miss. The infrastructure direction made progress: a TPU-native sampler and latent-topic discovery path were prototyped, and smoke runs wrote reusable artifacts. The main scientific result so far is negative for tokenizer-vocab bigrams: both `r1` and `r2` completed, but Qwen collapsed bare two-word prompts into generic explanatory continuations, with 43/48 prompts sharing the same first token in at least 75% of samples and no useful improvement from expanding from the original prompt. Do not keep tuning the content-word bigram path; if this line continues, use a weaker launch family or a scorer that discounts generic preambles and validates candidates with the pairwise BPB gap workflow.

### Helpful links
- Initial sampler implementation note: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5006#issuecomment-4307017787
- First latent-topic smoke: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5006#issuecomment-4316637640
- Bigram `r1` result: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5006#issuecomment-4316819223
- Bigram dead-end decision: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5006#issuecomment-4317162165
<!-- experiment-tldr:end -->

## Description
Use free generation from strong base models as an eval-discovery tool for pretraining blind spots. Start with Qwen3, then compare against Llama, Gemma, and other strong bases where available. The goal is to find surface-form families that strong models naturally continue but Marin may not cover well in Paloma, uncheatable evals, raw technical text, or capability eval slices.

This is hypothesis generation, not evidence by itself. Any sampled category should be checked against real held-out documents and then validated with pairwise gap/PPL before changing data mixtures.

## Hypothesis or Goal
Sampling with both empty prompts and seeded prefixes will surface missing or under-covered distributions such as raw URLs, package metadata, tables, logs, schemas, notebooks, compiler output, non-English technical docs, citations, mixed prose-code formats, and unusual whitespace/layout patterns. Agent-assisted clustering can turn samples into candidate eval slices, but each cluster needs a real source and a coverage decision: already covered, add eval only, add data work, or ignore.

* Parent confidence epic: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5005
* Gap finder: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/4934
* Raw technical text: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/4961

comments.body: @weaverbot are we using latent attention in the grug "hero" model today? My impression was that we switched to latent attention & KDA as part of the MFU optimization work

On it — https://loom.oa.dev/s/cqjz8hvy
[marin-style-nightly-updates](https://loom.oa.dev/s/cqjz8hvy/artifacts/marin-style-nightly-updates)

- 🟢 `Oct 16 16:32Z` Answered issue #6494: hero uses GQA; KDA/MLA are in fast_track experiments. https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6494#issuecomment-6220057604

🤖 No. The current Grug production hero (`hero-ctx16k-step257k`) uses GQA softmax attention, with 48 query heads, 12 local KV heads, and 6 global KV heads. Its [attention module](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L538-L578) has separate Q, K, and V projections; the [hero recipe](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/heuristic.py#L85-L115) selects the FA4 kernel. The recipe's `latent_dim=3072` is [LatentMoE](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L1102-L1115): it compresses expert-parallel transport, not the attention KV cache.

The [MFU handoff](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9960) moved the hero to an optimized MoE stack; the earlier [FA4 handoff](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9378) changed its attention kernel. Neither switched its attention architecture to MLA or Kimi Delta Attention (KDA). The combination of KDA on local layers and MLA on global layers is being tested in the separate [`fast_track` ladder](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9451), whose first version explicitly excludes hero-scale speed testing. The latest [hero handoff](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10101) changed context length and QK scaling while retaining the GQA recipe.

MLA is not on the hero- it is on Marin Belay and running at 28 MFU at hero scale. https://claude.ai/artifact/2ZfzxTKZBMF3HJ77xeSQb5.

So now that it has competitive MFU, can give it a fair shot for future runs. Will need to test further to see if its better. Interestingly, Western labs like Meta (at least their open release), reflection, and microsoft seem to be sticking with GQA. And then there is Deepseek who is off doing their own unique attention stuff.

I will test the conversion idea. I think for the scale of models we will train, qk-norm on MLA head may be fine.

topics.title: Experiment: Pallas Mosaic MGPU fused MoE dispatch + W13/SiLU
topics.body:
🤖
<!-- experiment-tldr:start -->
## Summary

This experiment is building a DeepEP-free single-node EP8 Grug MoE path using Pallas Mosaic MGPU remote refs, with fused routed-token dispatch into expert-major tiles followed by W13/SiLU expert compute on 8xH100. The first handoff established the spec, baselines, and implementation path; the latest validation added a prepacked dispatch oracle, a shard-local remote-ref validation primitive, and a local fused W13/SiLU Pallas kernel. H100x8 smoke runs now show exact dispatch payload/metadata parity for top-k 1 and top-k 4, with W13/SiLU max error 2 in bf16, so the immediate remaining work is tiled/staged dispatch plus backward/custom-VJP coverage before any training integration claim.

### Helpful links
- Spec branch handoff: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6597#issuecomment-4783570735
- Scope assessment and relevant MoE backends: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6597#issuecomment-4783575997
- Milestones 1 and 2 H100 validation update: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6597#issuecomment-4783991292
<!-- experiment-tldr:end -->

## Scope

Target hardware: one 8xH100 NVLink island first; future NVL72/GB200 is the medium-term motivation.

Target backend: a new experimental Grug MoE backend, likely mosaic_mgpu, wired next to ring/ragged_all_to_all under lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe. Do not use DeepEP, NCCL EP, FFI transport, NIC, RDMA, or NVSHMEM for this path.

Primary spec branch: codex/pallas-mosaic-mgpu-moe-spec

Spec path on branch: .agents/projects/pallas_mosaic_mgpu_moe_spec.md

Research logbook path: .agents/logbooks/pallas-mosaic-mgpu-moe.md

## Hypothesis or Goal

A Pallas Mosaic MGPU kernel can route token blocks directly into destination expert-major tiles and consume them with W13/SiLU, avoiding the wrapper/permutation/opaque-FFI costs that made DeepEP hard to profile and unreliable.

The first validation slice is remote dispatch layout correctness. The first product milestone is fused dispatch + W13/SiLU for top-k 4 on EP8. The training milestone requires a custom VJP/backward path and fwd+bwd+SGD profile.

## Current Baselines

- DeepEP EP16/N2 B64 save_moe May387 reached about 17 MFU, but DeepEP has repeatedly hit recv-counter timeouts.
- EP8/B16 readable profiles May363/May378 showed MoE around 37-40% of step time.
- Ring/ragged A2A remain more debuggable than DeepEP, but ragged_all_to_all was slower than ring in the tested shape.
- SonicMoE is included as a local expert compute/layout reference, not an EP transport reference.

## Required Deliverables

- Readable JAX reference for routing/layout and forward math.
- Pallas Mosaic MGPU remote dispatch validation slice.
- Fused dispatch + W13/SiLU kernel for top-k 4.
- W_down and combine path sufficient for full forward parity.
- Custom VJP plan and small-shape gradient parity before training claims.
- Performance harness reporting prepack, dispatch, W13, SiLU, W2, combine, backward W13/SiLU, and backward transport.
- Comparison against ring and ragged_all_to_all on the same single-node shape.

## Decision Log

- 2026-06-23: Start with 8xH100 single-node EP8. Keep DeepEP out of this path; it is a baseline only.
- 2026-06-23: Product target is fused dispatch + W13/SiLU. Dispatch-only exists only as a validation slice.
- 2026-06-23: Include backward/custom VJP in the plan before training integration.

## Negative Results Index

- DeepEP May391 fixed-metadata profile attempt failed on step 1 with internode recv-counter timeouts before producing a useful profile.
- Prior DeepEP targeted offload variants also hit recv-counter timeouts or underperformed.

## Completion Criteria

- EP8 single-node 8xH100 fused dispatch + W13/SiLU works for top-k 4.
- Values match a JAX reference and one existing backend on small and realistic shapes.
- A custom VJP exists and passes small-shape gradient parity, even if the first backward implementation is reference/JAX rather than Mosaic.
- A fwd+bwd+SGD profile runs with model_axis=1 and phase-attributed named scopes.
- The report compares against ring and ragged_all_to_all on the same shape.
